title.raw: 卷四百五十一 列傳第二百一十 忠義六 趙良淳徐道隆 姜才 馬塈 密佑 張世傑 陸秀夫 徐應鑣 陳文龍 鄧得遇 張珏 Volume 451 Biographies 210: Loyalty and Righteousness 6 - Zhaoliang Chunxu Daolong, Jiang Cai, Ma Ji, Mi You, Zhang Shijie, Lu Xiufu, Xu Yingbiao, Chen Wenlong, Deng Deyu, Zhang Jue

sentences.zh: 忠義六

translations.literal: Loyalty and Righteousness 6
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty and Righteousness 6

sentences.zh: ○趙良淳

translations.literal: ○ Zhao Liangchun
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Liangchun

sentences.zh: （徐道隆）〉

translations.literal: (Xu Daolong)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Xu Daolong)

sentences.zh: 薑才馬塈密佑張世傑陸秀夫徐應鑣陳文龍鄧得遇張玨

translations.literal: Jiang Cai, Ma Ji, Mi You, Zhang Shijie, Lu Xiufu, Xu Yingbiao, Chen Wenlong, Deng Deyu, Zhang Jue
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Cai, Ma Ji, Mi You, Zhang Shijie, Lu Xiufu, Xu Yingbiao, Chen Wenlong, Deng Deyu, and Zhang Jue

sentences.zh: 趙良淳，字景程，居饒之餘幹，太宗子恭憲王之後，丞相汝愚曾孫也。

translations.literal: Zhao Liangchun, courtesy name Jingcheng, lived in Yugan in Rao Prefecture. He was a descendant of Prince Gongxian, a son of Emperor Taizong, and a great-grandson of the chief minister Zhao Ruyu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Liangchun, whose courtesy name was Jingcheng, came from Yugan in Rao Prefecture. He was descended from Prince Gongxian, a son of Emperor Taizong of Song, and was the great-grandson of Chief Minister Zhao Ruyu.

sentences.zh: 累世以學行名，號賢宗子。

translations.literal: For generations his family was famed for learning and conduct, and was called a worthy imperial clansman.
translations.idiomatic: His family had been renowned for generations for scholarship and moral conduct, and was known as a model branch of the imperial house.

sentences.zh: 良淳少學於其鄉先生饒魯，知立身大節。

translations.literal: In youth Liangchun studied under his local teacher Rao Lu and learned the great principles of how to stand in life.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Liangchun studied under the local scholar Rao Lu and learned the cardinal principles of personal integrity.

sentences.zh: 及仕，所至以幹治稱，而未嚐幹人薦舉。

translations.literal: When he entered office, wherever he served he was praised for capable administration, yet he never sought to push himself forward through recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office he won praise everywhere he served for capable administration, yet he never pressed others for promotion.

sentences.zh: 初以蔭為泰寧主簿，三遷至淮西運轄，浮湛冗官二十餘年。

translations.literal: At first, through hereditary privilege, he became registrar of Taining; after three promotions he reached transport commissioner in Huai West, drifting in minor posts for more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered service by hereditary privilege as registrar of Taining, rose through three promotions to transport commissioner in Huai West, and spent more than twenty years adrift in undistinguished posts.

sentences.zh: 馬光祖、李伯玉、範丁孫交薦辟之，卒不振拔。

translations.literal: Ma Guangzu, Li Boyu, and Fan Dingsun repeatedly recommended and summoned him, yet in the end he was never raised up.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Guangzu, Li Boyu, and Fan Dingsun all recommended him in turn, yet he was never advanced.

sentences.zh: 考舉及格，改知分寧縣。

translations.literal: He passed the examination and was changed to magistrate of Fenning County.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the civil service examination he was appointed magistrate of Fenning County.

sentences.zh: 分寧，江西劇邑，俗尚嘩訐，良淳治之，不用刑戮，不任吏胥，取民之敦孝者，身親尊禮之，至甚傑驁者，乃繩以法，俗為少革。

translations.literal: Fenning was a difficult county in Jiangxi, where custom favored clamor and litigation. Liangchun governed it without using punishments of death, without relying on clerks and runners; he selected among the people those who were earnest in filial piety and personally honored them, and only when men were extremely fierce and arrogant did he bind them with law. Custom was somewhat reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Fenning was a notoriously difficult county in Jiangxi, where quarrelsome litigation was the norm. Liangchun governed without executions and without leaning on clerks and runners. He singled out the most dutiful among the people and honored them in person; only the most violent and defiant he brought under the law. The local ways improved somewhat.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，特差權江西安撫司機宜文字，詔除諸司審計院，督餉江西，升大理司直。

translations.literal: When his term ended he was specially assigned as acting confidential clerk of the Jiangxi Pacification Commission, then by edict appointed to the Bureau of Audits for Various Offices, supervising grain transport in Jiangxi, and promoted to direct secretary of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired he was specially assigned as acting confidential clerk on the Jiangxi Pacification Commission, then appointed by edict to the Bureau of Audits for Various Offices to supervise grain shipments in Jiangxi, and promoted to direct secretary of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 鹹淳末，廷臣議眾建宗室於內郡，以為屏翰，遂除良淳知安吉州。

translations.literal: At the end of the Xianchun era court ministers discussed broadly establishing imperial clansmen in inner prefectures as protective screens, and so Liangchun was appointed prefect of Anji.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Xianchun reign, court ministers proposed posting many imperial clansmen in interior prefectures as a defensive screen, and Liangchun was accordingly appointed prefect of Anji.

sentences.zh: 先是，知州李庚遁，百事隳廢。

translations.literal: Earlier the prefect Li Geng had fled, and every affair lay in ruin.
translations.idiomatic: The previous prefect, Li Geng, had fled, leaving every branch of government in collapse.

sentences.zh: 良淳至，日與僚吏論所以守禦之備，悉舉行之。

translations.literal: When Liangchun arrived, day by day he discussed with his staff the measures needed for defense and put them all into practice.
translations.idiomatic: On his arrival Liangchun met daily with his staff to plan the city's defenses and carried every measure through.

sentences.zh: 時歲饑，民相聚為盜，所在蜂起。

translations.literal: At the time the year was famine-struck; the people gathered and became bandits, rising everywhere like swarms of bees.
translations.idiomatic: Famine gripped the land, and people banded together as robbers, outbreaks flaring up everywhere.

sentences.zh: 或請以兵擊之，良淳曰：“民豈樂為盜哉？

translations.literal: Some asked to strike them with troops. Liangchun said, "Would the people delight in becoming bandits?
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him to send troops against them. Liangchun said, "Do you think the people enjoy becoming bandits?

sentences.zh: 時艱歲旱，故相率剽掠苟活耳。

translations.literal: Times are hard and the year is drought-struck; therefore they follow one another in plundering merely to stay alive."
translations.idiomatic: Times are desperate and the harvest has failed—they band together to loot only so they can survive."

sentences.zh: ”命僚屬以義諭之，眾皆投兵散歸，其不歸者眾縛以獻。

translations.literal: He ordered his subordinates to admonish them with righteousness; the multitude all cast down their weapons and dispersed home, and those who did not return were bound by the crowd and presented.
translations.idiomatic: He had his subordinates reason with them on moral grounds. The crowds threw down their weapons and went home; those who refused were seized by the people themselves and handed over.

sentences.zh: 有掠人貨財詣其主謝過而還之者。

translations.literal: There were some who, having plundered people's goods and wealth, went to their owners to apologize and returned them.
translations.idiomatic: Some who had robbed others even came forward to apologize to their victims and returned what they had taken.

sentences.zh: 良淳勸富人出粟振之，嚐語人曰：“使太守身可以濟民，亦所不惜也。

translations.literal: Liangchun urged the wealthy to bring out grain to relieve them, and once said to people, "If the prefect's own person could relieve the people, that too would not be spared."
translations.idiomatic: Liangchun urged the wealthy to donate grain for relief, and once told the people, "If giving my own body could save the people, I would not hesitate to do it."

sentences.zh: ”其言懇懇，足以動人，人皆倒囷以應之。

translations.literal: His words were earnest and sufficient to move people; everyone overturned their granaries to respond.
translations.idiomatic: His words were so earnest that they moved everyone; people emptied their granaries in response.

sentences.zh: 朝議尋以徐道隆為浙西提刑，以輔良淳，加良淳直秘閣。

translations.literal: The court soon appointed Xu Daolong as judicial commissioner of Zhe West to assist Liangchun, and added for Liangchun the title of direct attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The court soon named Xu Daolong judicial commissioner of Zhe West to assist Liangchun and granted Liangchun the title of direct attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 文天祥去平江，潰兵四出剽掠，良淳捕斬數人，梟首市中，兵稍戢。

translations.literal: When Wen Tianxiang left Pingjiang, routed troops went out in all directions to plunder. Liangchun captured and executed several, displayed their heads in the market, and the soldiers were somewhat restrained.
translations.idiomatic: After Wen Tianxiang withdrew from Pingjiang, routed soldiers fanned out to plunder. Liangchun seized and executed several, displayed their heads in the marketplace, and the troops quieted somewhat.

sentences.zh: 已而範文虎遣使持書招降，良淳焚書斬其使。

translations.literal: Before long Fan Wenhu sent an envoy bearing a letter to summon surrender; Liangchun burned the letter and executed the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Fan Wenhu sent an envoy with a letter offering surrender terms. Liangchun burned the letter and beheaded the messenger.

sentences.zh: 大兵迫獨鬆關，有旨趣道隆入衛。

translations.literal: The great army pressed Dusong Pass, and there was an edict urging Daolong to enter the capital for defense.
translations.idiomatic: As the Mongol army closed on Dusong Pass, an edict ordered Xu Daolong to hurry to the capital for its defense.

sentences.zh: 道隆既去，大兵至，軍其東西門。

translations.literal: After Daolong had gone, the great army arrived and encamped at its eastern and western gates.
translations.idiomatic: Once Daolong had departed, the enemy army arrived and invested the eastern and western gates.

sentences.zh: 良淳率眾城守，夜就茇舍陴上，不歸。

translations.literal: Liangchun led the multitude in defending the city; at night he lodged on the thatched shelter atop the parapet and did not return home.
translations.idiomatic: Liangchun led the defense of the city himself, sleeping each night on the ramparts in a thatched shelter and never going home.

sentences.zh: 先是，朝廷遣將吳國定援宜興，宜興已危，不敢往，乃如安吉見良淳，願留以為輔。

translations.literal: Earlier the court had sent the general Wu Guoding to relieve Yixing. Yixing was already in peril and he dared not go; instead he came to Anji to see Liangchun and asked to remain as his assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the court had dispatched General Wu Guoding to relieve Yixing. Finding Yixing already beyond saving, he did not dare proceed but came instead to Anji to see Liangchun and asked to stay on as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 良淳見國定慷慨大言，意其可用也，請於朝，留戍安吉。

translations.literal: Liangchun saw Guoding speak boldly and generously and thought him usable; he requested of the court that Guoding be left to garrison Anji.
translations.idiomatic: Impressed by Guoding's bold and impassioned words, Liangchun judged him useful and petitioned the court to leave him garrisoned at Anji.

sentences.zh: 已而國定開南門納外兵，兵入城呼曰：“眾散，元帥不殺汝。

translations.literal: Before long Guoding opened the south gate and admitted the foreign troops. The soldiers entered the city and shouted, "Disperse—the marshal will not kill you."
translations.idiomatic: Before long Guoding opened the south gate and let the enemy in. The troops entered shouting, "Scatter! The marshal will not harm you."

sentences.zh: ”於是眾號泣散去。

translations.literal: Thereupon the multitude wailed and dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders broke down in tears and scattered.

sentences.zh: 良淳命車歸府，兵士止之曰：“事至此，侍郎當為自全計。

translations.literal: Liangchun ordered his carriage to return to the prefectural residence. Soldiers stopped him, saying, "Things have come to this—the Vice Minister ought to plan for his own preservation."
translations.idiomatic: Liangchun ordered his carriage back to the prefectural compound. Soldiers barred his way, saying, "Matters have come to this, my lord—you must think of saving yourself."

sentences.zh: ”良淳叱去之。

translations.literal: Liangchun shouted them away.
translations.idiomatic: Liangchun shouted them away.

sentences.zh: 命家人出避，乃閉閣自經。

translations.literal: He ordered his household to go out and take refuge, then shut his chamber and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his family away to safety, shut himself in his chamber, and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 有兵士解救之，復蘇，眾羅拜泣曰：“侍郎何自苦？

translations.literal: Some soldiers rescued him and he revived. The crowd bowed around him weeping and said, "Vice Minister, why torment yourself?
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers cut him down and revived him. They knelt around him in tears, crying, "My lord, why do you torment yourself?

sentences.zh: 逃之猶可求生。

translations.literal: If you flee, you may still seek life."
translations.idiomatic: If you flee, you can still live."

sentences.zh: ”良淳叱曰：“我豈逃生者邪？

translations.literal: Liangchun shouted, "Am I one who flees to save his life?"
translations.idiomatic: Liangchun roared, "Do you think I am a man who runs away to save his skin?"

sentences.zh: ”眾猶環守不去，良淳大呼曰：“爾輩欲為亂邪？

translations.literal: The crowd still ringed him and would not leave. Liangchun shouted loudly, "Do you lot wish to make trouble?"
translations.idiomatic: They still crowded around him and would not leave. Liangchun bellowed, "Are you trying to start a riot?"

sentences.zh: ”眾涕泣出，復投繯而死。

translations.literal: The crowd wept and went out; he again cast the noose and died.
translations.idiomatic: They left in tears. He hanged himself again and died.

sentences.zh: 徐道隆字伯謙，婺州武義人。

translations.literal: Xu Daolong, courtesy name Boqian, was a man of Wuyi in Wu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Daolong, whose courtesy name was Boqian, came from Wuyi in Wu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父煥，知南雄。

translations.literal: His father Huan was prefect of Nanxiong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xu Huan had served as prefect of Nanxiong.

sentences.zh: 道隆以任入官，累官潭州判官、權知全州。

translations.literal: Daolong entered office through appointment and successively served as judge of Tan Prefecture and acting prefect of Quan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Daolong entered service by direct appointment and rose to judge of Tan Prefecture and acting prefect of Quan.

sentences.zh: 荊湖製置使汪立信奏辟道隆為參議官。

translations.literal: Wang Lixin, pacification commissioner of Jinghu and Hubei, memorialized to summon Daolong as deliberation officer.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lixin, pacification commissioner of Jinghu and Hubei, recommended Daolong for appointment as deliberation officer.

sentences.zh: 立信遷兵部尚書，道隆與賓客十許人俱去江陵。

translations.literal: When Lixin was transferred to Minister of War, Daolong went with some ten-odd guests and left Jiangling together.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Lixin was promoted to Minister of War, Daolong accompanied him to Jiangling along with a dozen or so retainers.

sentences.zh: 趙孟傳為製置使，以道隆參其軍事，遂為提點刑獄。

translations.literal: Zhao Mengchuan became pacification commissioner, employed Daolong in his military affairs, and he then became judicial intendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Mengchuan became pacification commissioner he took Daolong onto his staff for military affairs, and Daolong was eventually made judicial intendant.

sentences.zh: 時文天祥既去平江，潰卒四出，為浙西患苦，安吉尤甚。

translations.literal: At the time Wen Tianxiang had already left Pingjiang; routed soldiers went out in all directions and became a scourge to Zhe West, Anji especially.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Tianxiang had already withdrawn from Pingjiang, and routed soldiers spread across Zhe West, Anji suffering worst of all.

sentences.zh: 有旨令道隆措置，乃梟其首亂者於市。

translations.literal: There was an edict ordering Daolong to handle the situation; he then displayed the heads of the chief troublemakers in the market.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Daolong to restore order; he executed the ringleaders and displayed their heads in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 牛監軍遁，範文虎、程鵬飛、管景模俱遺書誘降，道隆焚書斬使。

translations.literal: Niu Jianjun fled. Fan Wenhu, Cheng Pengfei, and Guan Jingmo all sent letters to entice surrender; Daolong burned the letters and executed the envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Niu fled. Fan Wenhu, Cheng Pengfei, and Guan Jingmo each sent letters urging surrender; Daolong burned every letter and beheaded the messengers.

sentences.zh: 大兵至臨平皋亭山，令間道入援，時水陸皆有屯軍，道絕不通，議由太湖經武康、臨安縣境勤王。

translations.literal: The great army reached Gaoting Mountain at Linping and ordered him to enter by a side road to relieve the throne. At the time both land and water had encamped troops and the routes were wholly cut; it was discussed to go by way of Lake Tai through Wukang and the territory of Lin'an County to aid the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy reached Gaoting Mountain near Linping and ordered him to march by a side road to relieve the capital. Land and water routes were both blocked by enemy camps, so he resolved to reach the emperor by way of Lake Tai through Wukang and Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 即日乘舟出臨湖門，泊宋村。

translations.literal: That same day he took boat out through Linhu Gate and moored at Song Village.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he put out by boat through Linhu Gate and anchored at Song Village.

sentences.zh: 郡守趙良淳既縊死。

translations.literal: The prefect Zhao Liangchun had already hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: By then Prefect Zhao Liangchun had already taken his own life.

sentences.zh: 德祐二年正月朔旦，追兵及道隆，江陵親從軍三百人殊死戰，矢盡槍槊折，一軍盡沒。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month of the second year of Deyou, pursuing troops overtook Daolong. Three hundred personal followers from Jiangling fought to the death; arrows were exhausted and spears and pikes broken, and the whole force was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the first month of Deyou 1276, pursuers caught Daolong. His three hundred Jiangling guards fought to the last man—arrows spent, spears shattered—until the entire force was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 道隆見執艦內，間守者少怠，赴水死，長子載孫亦赴水死。

translations.literal: Daolong was captured inside the ship; when the guards slackened slightly he threw himself into the water and died, and his eldest son Zaisun also threw himself into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: Daolong was seized aboard his ship. When his guards relaxed their watch he leapt into the water and drowned; his eldest son Zaisun drowned himself as well.

sentences.zh: 餘兵有脫歸者言於朝，命贈官賜諡，厚恤其家，立廟安吉，官其子孫。

translations.literal: Surviving soldiers who escaped and returned reported to the court; he was ordered posthumous office and a posthumous title, his family richly compensated, a temple established at Anji, and his sons and grandsons given office.
translations.idiomatic: Survivors who made it back reported to court. He was granted posthumous rank and a posthumous title, his family richly compensated, a temple raised at Anji, and offices given to his descendants.

sentences.zh: 越三日宋亡。

translations.literal: Three days later Song perished.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later the Song dynasty fell.

sentences.zh: 薑才，濠州人。

translations.literal: Jiang Cai was a man of Hao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Cai came from Hao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 貌短悍。

translations.literal: In appearance he was short and fierce.
translations.idiomatic: He was short in stature and fierce in bearing.

sentences.zh: 少被掠入河朔，稍長亡歸，隸淮南兵中，以善戰名，然以來歸人不得大官，為通州副都統。

translations.literal: In youth he was carried off into Hebei and Shandong; when somewhat grown he fled back, was enrolled among the Huainan troops, and was famed for skill in battle, yet because he was a returned captive he could not obtain high office and served as vice commander-in-chief of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was captured and taken north to the Yellow River region. When he grew older he escaped and rejoined the Huainan army, winning fame as a fighter. Because he was a man who had returned from captivity, however, he was never given high rank and remained only vice commander-in-chief at Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 時淮多健將，然驍雄無逾才。

translations.literal: At the time Huai had many strong generals, yet in fierce valor none surpassed Cai.
translations.idiomatic: Huai had many able generals at the time, but none matched Cai in raw fighting prowess.

sentences.zh: 才知兵，善騎射，撫士卒有恩，至臨陣，軍律凜凜。

translations.literal: Cai understood warfare, was skilled in mounted archery, and treated soldiers with kindness; yet when he reached the battlefield military discipline was stern and awe-inspiring.
translations.idiomatic: Cai understood warfare, excelled at mounted archery, and treated his men with genuine kindness—yet on the battlefield his discipline was iron and terrifying.

sentences.zh: 其子當戰，回白事，才望見以為敗也，拔劍馳逐，幾殺之。

translations.literal: When his son was in battle and turned back to report, Cai saw him from afar and thought it defeat; he drew his sword and galloped in pursuit, nearly killing him.
translations.idiomatic: Once during battle his son turned back to report. Cai saw him from a distance, mistook it for a rout, drew his sword, and galloped after him, nearly killing his own son.

sentences.zh: 賈似道出師，才以兵屬孫虎臣為先鋒，相拒於丁家洲。

translations.literal: When Jia Sidao led the army out, Cai placed his troops under Sun Huchen as vanguard and faced the enemy at Dingjiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Jia Sidao took the field, Cai attached his force to Sun Huchen's vanguard and met the enemy at Dingjiazhou.

sentences.zh: 大軍設炮架彀車弩江濱，中流數千艘，旌旗聯亙，鼓行而下。

translations.literal: The great army set up cannon frames, ballista carts, and crossbows along the riverbank; in midstream were several thousand vessels, banners and flags stretching in unbroken lines, advancing to the beat of drums.
translations.idiomatic: The Mongol army lined the shore with cannon platforms, ballista wagons, and crossbows, while thousands of ships filled the midstream, banners unbroken from bank to bank, advancing to the beat of drums.

sentences.zh: 才奮兵前接戰，鋒已交，虎臣遽過其妾所乘舟，眾見之，歡曰：“步帥遁矣。

translations.literal: Cai roused his troops and advanced to join battle. The fronts had already met when Huchen suddenly passed the boat on which his concubine rode. The multitude saw it and shouted, "The infantry commander has fled!"
translations.idiomatic: Cai threw his men forward to engage. The lines had barely met when Huchen was seen steering toward the boat carrying his concubine. The troops cried out, "The infantry commander is running away!"

sentences.zh: ”於是諸軍皆潰，才亦收兵入揚州。

translations.literal: Thereupon all armies collapsed, and Cai also gathered his troops and entered Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Every unit broke. Cai too gathered what he could and withdrew into Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 大兵乘勝攻揚州，才為三疊陣逆之三里溝，戰有功。

translations.literal: The great army pressed its victory and attacked Yangzhou. Cai formed a triple-ranked array to oppose them at Sanligou and fought with merit.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy pressed their advantage against Yangzhou. Cai met them at Sanligou in a triple-ranked formation and fought them to a standstill.

sentences.zh: 又與元帥戰揚子橋，日暮兵亂，流矢貫才肩，才拔矢揮刀而前，所向辟易。

translations.literal: Again he fought the marshal at Yangzi Bridge. At dusk the army fell into disorder; a stray arrow pierced Cai's shoulder. Cai pulled out the arrow, waved his blade, and advanced; wherever he went the enemy gave way.
translations.idiomatic: He fought the enemy commander again at Yangzi Bridge. At dusk his lines buckled; a stray arrow drove through his shoulder. Cai pulled it out, raised his blade, and charged—wherever he went the enemy scattered.

sentences.zh: 已而大軍築長圍，自揚子橋竟瓜洲，東北跨灣頭至黃塘，西北至丁村，務欲以久困之，時德祐元年也。

translations.literal: Before long the great army built a long encirclement from Yangzi Bridge all the way to Guazhou, stretching northeast from Wantou to Huangtang and northwest to Ding Village, striving to wear them down over time. It was the first year of Deyou.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy then threw a long siege line from Yangzi Bridge to Guazhou, northeast from Wantou to Huangtang and northwest to Ding Village, intending to starve Yangzhou out. This was the first year of Deyou.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，宋亡。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year Song perished.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year the Song fell.

sentences.zh: 二月，五奉使及一閣門宣讚舍人持謝太后詔來諭降，才發弩射卻之，復以兵擊五奉使於召伯堡，大戰而退。

translations.literal: In the second month the Five Commissioners and one Gate Attendant and Proclamation Aide came bearing Empress Dowager Xie's edict to announce surrender. Cai loosed crossbows and drove them back, then again struck the Five Commissioners at Zhaobo Fort in a great battle and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the Five Commissioners and a Gate Attendant arrived with Empress Dowager Xie's edict demanding surrender. Cai drove them off with crossbow fire, then attacked them again at Zhaobo Fort in a fierce battle before pulling back.

sentences.zh: 未幾，瀛國公至瓜洲，才與庭芝泣涕誓將士出奪之。

translations.literal: Before long the Duke of Ying arrived at Guazhou. Cai and Tingzhi wept and swore before the officers and soldiers that they would go out to seize him back.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the young Emperor Gong arrived at Guazhou. Cai and Li Tingzhi wept before their troops and swore to rescue him.

sentences.zh: 將士皆感泣。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers were all moved to tears.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and men alike wept at the oath.

sentences.zh: 乃盡散金帛犒兵，以四萬人夜搗瓜洲，戰三時，眾擁瀛國公避去。

translations.literal: They then distributed all gold and silks to reward the troops and, with forty thousand men, raided Guazhou by night. They fought for three watches; the multitude shielded the Duke of Ying and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: They spent their gold and silk to reward the troops, then sent forty thousand men in a night assault on Guazhou. After three watches of fighting the enemy shielded the young emperor and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 才追戰至浦子市，夜猶不退。

translations.literal: Cai pursued the battle to Puzi Market and even at night did not withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Cai pursued as far as Puzi Market and fought on through the night without resting.

sentences.zh: 阿術使人招之，才曰：“吾寧死，豈作降將軍邪！

translations.literal: Azhu sent men to summon him. Cai said, "I would rather die—how could I become a surrendering general!"
translations.idiomatic: Azhu sent envoys to win him over. Cai said, "I would rather die than become a general who surrenders!"

sentences.zh: ”四月，才以兵攻灣頭柵。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Cai attacked the Wantou stockade with troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he attacked the Wantou stockade.

sentences.zh: 五月，復攻之，騎旋濘而止，乃舍騎步戰，至四鼓，全師以歸。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he attacked again; the cavalry wheeled in the mire and halted, so he abandoned horses and fought on foot until the fourth watch, then brought the whole army back.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he attacked again. His cavalry bogged down in the mud, so he dismounted and fought on foot until the fourth watch, then withdrew the whole force intact.

sentences.zh: 揚食盡，才時出運米真州、高郵以給兵。

translations.literal: Yangzhou's grain was exhausted; Cai from time to time went out to transport rice from Zhen Prefecture and Gaoyou to supply the troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Yangzhou ran out of food, Cai slipped out repeatedly to bring grain from Zhenzhou and Gaoyou to feed his men.

sentences.zh: 六月，護餉至馬家渡，萬戶史弼將兵擊奪之，才與戰達旦，弼幾殆，阿術馳兵來援，乃得免去。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, while escorting provisions to Majia Ford, the ten-thousand-household commander Shi Bi led troops to strike and seize them. Cai fought until dawn; Bi was nearly killed, but Azhu galloped troops to relieve him and only then was Cai able to escape.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, while escorting grain to Majia Ford, he was attacked by the Mongol commander Shi Bi. They fought until dawn; Bi was nearly killed before Azhu rode to his rescue and Cai barely got away.

sentences.zh: 庭芝以在圍久。

translations.literal: Tingzhi, because the siege had lasted long.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tingzhi had been under siege for a long time.

sentences.zh: 召才計事，屏左右，語久之，第聞才厲聲云：“相公不過忍片時痛耳。

translations.literal: He summoned Cai to plan affairs, dismissed those at hand, and spoke for a long time; those nearby only heard Cai say in a stern voice, "The Chancellor need only endure a moment's pain."
translations.idiomatic: He called Cai in to counsel him, dismissed everyone else, and spoke at length; those outside heard only Cai's stern voice: "My lord, you need only endure a moment's pain."

sentences.zh: ”左右聞之俱汗下。

translations.literal: Those at hand who heard it all broke into sweat.
translations.idiomatic: Those who overheard broke out in a cold sweat.

sentences.zh: 才自是以兵護庭芝第，期與俱死。

translations.literal: From then on Cai used troops to guard Tingzhi's residence, expecting to die together with him.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Cai posted troops to guard Li Tingzhi's residence, resolved to die with him.

sentences.zh: 七月，益王在福州，以龍神四廂都指揮使、保康軍承宣使召才，才與庭芝東至泰州，將入海。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the Prince of Yi was at Fuzhou and summoned Cai with the titles of commander of the four wings of the Dragon Spirit Guard and commissioner of the Baokang Army. Cai and Tingzhi went east to Taizhou, intending to put to sea.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Prince Yi at Fuzhou summoned Cai as commander of the Dragon Spirit Guard and commissioner of the Baokang Army. Cai and Li Tingzhi marched east to Taizhou, planning to escape by sea.

sentences.zh: 阿術以兵追及，圍泰州，使使者招之降，才不聽。

translations.literal: Azhu pursued with troops, besieged Taizhou, and sent envoys to summon surrender; Cai would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Azhu caught up, invested Taizhou, and sent envoys offering terms. Cai refused.

sentences.zh: 阿術驅揚兵士妻子至城下，會才疽發脅不能戰，諸將遂開門降。

translations.literal: Azhu drove the Yangzhou soldiers' wives and children to below the walls. It happened that Cai's carbuncle broke out on his flank and he could not fight; the generals then opened the gates and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Azhu drove the wives and children of the Yangzhou garrison before the walls. Cai's abscess flared on his side and left him unable to fight; his generals opened the gates and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 都統曹安國入才臥內，執之以獻。

translations.literal: The commander-in-chief Cao Anguo entered Cai's sleeping quarters and seized him to present.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Cao Anguo entered Cai's sickroom and seized him to present to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 阿術愛其忠勇，欲降而用之，才肆為慢言；

translations.literal: Azhu admired his loyalty and valor and wished to accept his surrender and employ him; Cai freely uttered insolent words.
translations.idiomatic: Azhu admired his loyalty and courage and wanted to win him over, but Cai heaped insults on him.

sentences.zh: 阿術責庭芝不降，才曰：“不降者才也。

translations.literal: Azhu reproached Tingzhi for not surrendering. Cai said, "The one who would not surrender is Cai."
translations.idiomatic: When Azhu blamed Li Tingzhi for refusing to surrender, Cai said, "I am the one who would not surrender."

sentences.zh: ”復憤憤不已，阿術怒，剮之揚州。

translations.literal: He again raged without cease. Azhu was angry and dismembered him at Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He raged on without stopping. Azhu had him dismembered at Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 才臨刑，夏貴出其傍，才切齒曰：“若見我寧不愧死邪？

translations.literal: As Cai faced execution, Xia Gui appeared beside him. Cai gnashed his teeth and said, "When you see me, are you not ashamed to die?"
translations.idiomatic: At the execution Xia Gui appeared beside him. Cai ground his teeth and said, "Look at me—are you not ashamed to go on living?"

sentences.zh: 有洪福者，夏貴家僮也，從貴積勞為鎮巢雄江左軍統製，鎮江北。

translations.literal: There was one Hong Fu, a household slave of Xia Gui's, who through following Gui accumulated merit and became commander of the Zhenchao Xiong Jiangzuo Army, garrisoning north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: There was a man named Hong Fu, a household slave of Xia Gui's who through long service rose to command the Zhenchao army on the north bank of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 貴降，福與子大淵、大源、下班祗候彭元亮結貴軍復之，加右武大夫、知鎮巢。

translations.literal: When Gui surrendered, Fu with his sons Dayuan and Dayuan and the lower-rank attendant Peng Yuanliang rallied Gui's former troops to recover it; he was promoted to Right Martial Grand Master and made prefect of Zhenchao.
translations.idiomatic: When Xia Gui surrendered, Hong Fu with his sons Dayuan and Dayuan and attendant Peng Yuanliang rallied the old garrison and retook the fortress; he was made Right Martial Grand Master and prefect of Zhenchao.

sentences.zh: 貴既臣附，招福，不聽，使其從子往，福斬之。

translations.literal: After Gui had submitted as a subject, he summoned Fu, who would not listen; he sent his nephew, and Fu beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: After Xia Gui had submitted to the Mongols he sent envoys to win Hong Fu over. Fu refused; when Xia Gui sent a nephew, Fu executed him.

sentences.zh: 大兵攻城，久不拔，遣貴至城下，好語語福，請單騎入城。

translations.literal: The great army attacked the city for long without taking it and sent Gui to below the walls with kind words to Fu, asking to enter the city alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: The siege dragged on without success, so they sent Xia Gui to the walls with friendly words, asking to enter alone on horseback.

sentences.zh: 福信之，門發而伏兵起，執福父子，屠城中。

translations.literal: Fu believed him; when the gate opened ambush troops rose, seized Fu and his sons, and slaughtered within the city.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Fu believed him. The moment the gate opened, hidden troops rushed in, seized Hong Fu and his sons, and massacred the city.

sentences.zh: 貴涖殺，大源、大淵謔曰：“法止誅首謀，何至舉家為戮？

translations.literal: Gui came to supervise the killing. Dayuan and Dayuan jested, saying, "The law punishes only the chief plotter—why extend slaughter to the whole family?"
translations.idiomatic: When Xia Gui came to oversee the executions, his sons Dayuan and Dayuan joked, "The law punishes only the ringleader—why wipe out the entire family?"

sentences.zh: ”福叱曰：“以一命報宋朝，何至告人求活邪？

translations.literal: Fu shouted, "With one life I repay the Song dynasty—why would I tell others to beg for life?"
translations.idiomatic: Hong Fu snapped, "I am repaying the Song with my one life—why would I beg anyone to spare me?"

sentences.zh: ”次及福，福大罵數貴不忠，請身南向死，以明不背國也。

translations.literal: When it came to Fu's turn, Fu cursed Gui many times for disloyalty and asked to die facing south, to show he did not betray the state.
translations.idiomatic: When his turn came, Hong Fu cursed Xia Gui again and again for treachery and asked to die facing south, to show he had never betrayed his country.

sentences.zh: 聞者流涕。

translations.literal: Those who heard wept.
translations.idiomatic: All who witnessed it wept.

sentences.zh: 馬塈，宕昌人也。

translations.literal: Ma Ji was a man of Dangchang.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Ji came from Dangchang.

sentences.zh: 一家父叔兄弟皆以忠勇為名將，而塈與其兄堃特顯。

translations.literal: For generations father, uncles, and brothers were all famed generals for loyalty and valor, while Ji and his elder brother Kun were especially prominent.
translations.idiomatic: His family for generations had produced generals famed for loyalty and courage; Ji and his elder brother Kun stood out above the rest.

sentences.zh: 鹹淳中，塈知欽州，徙知邕。

translations.literal: During the Xianchun era Ji was prefect of Qin Prefecture and was transferred to be prefect of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianchun reign he served as prefect of Qin and was then transferred to Yong.

sentences.zh: 邕地接六詔、安南，傍通諸溪峒，撫禦少失宜，往往召亂。

translations.literal: Yong's territory bordered the Six Zhao and Annan and connected to the various stream gorges and cave settlements; if pacification and control were slightly mishandled, disorder was often invited.
translations.idiomatic: Yong bordered the Six Zhao kingdoms and Annan and opened onto countless mountain valleys and tribal domains; the slightest misstep in governance could spark rebellion.

sentences.zh: 塈鎮撫諸蠻及治關隘，皆有條理，大理不敢越善闡，安南不敢入永平，諸峒皆上帳冊，邊陲晏然。

translations.literal: Ji pacified the various tribes and administered the passes and barriers all with order; Dali did not dare cross Shanchan, Annan did not dare enter Yongping, every gorge submitted registers, and the frontier was tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Ji pacified the tribes and organized the frontier passes so thoroughly that Dali dared not cross Shanchan, Annan dared not enter Yongping, every gorge submitted its registers, and the borderlands knew peace.

sentences.zh: 廣西經略李興上其功，加閣門宣讚舍人。

translations.literal: Li Xing, pacification commissioner of Guangxi, memorialized his achievements and he was added as Gate Attendant and Proclamation Aide.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi Pacification Commissioner Li Xing reported his achievements to court, and he was promoted to Gate Attendant and Proclamation Aide.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以左武衛將軍征入朝。

translations.literal: Before long, as Left Martial Guard General, he was summoned to court.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was summoned to court as Left Martial Guard General.

sentences.zh: 已而宋亡，塈因留靜江，總屯戍諸軍，護經略司印守城。

translations.literal: Before long Song perished; Ji therefore remained at Jingjiang, commanding all garrison troops, guarding the seal of the pacification commission, and defending the city.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song fell he remained at Jingjiang, took command of all garrison forces, guarded the pacification commission's seal, and held the city.

sentences.zh: 至元十四年，平章阿裏海牙攻廣西。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhiyuan, the Grand Councillor Arighaiya attacked Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1277 Grand Councillor Arighaiya invaded Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 塈發所部及諸峒兵守靜江，而自將三千人守嚴關，鑿馬坑，斷嶺道。

translations.literal: Ji deployed his own troops and the gorge militias to defend Jingjiang, while he personally led three thousand men to hold Yanguan, dug horse pits, and cut the mountain road.
translations.idiomatic: Ji sent his own troops and tribal levies to defend Jingjiang while he personally led three thousand men to Yanguan, dug cavalry traps, and severed the mountain road.

sentences.zh: 大兵攻嚴關不克，乃以偏師入平樂，過臨桂，夾攻塈。

translations.literal: The great army could not take Yanguan and therefore sent a detached force into Pingle, passed through Lingui, and attacked Ji from both sides.
translations.idiomatic: The main army failed to take Yanguan, so a flanking force marched through Pingle and Lingui to attack Ji from two sides.

sentences.zh: 塈兵敗，退保靜江。

translations.literal: Ji's army was defeated and he withdrew to defend Jingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was defeated and fell back to Jingjiang.

sentences.zh: 平章使人招降，塈發弩射之。

translations.literal: The Grand Councillor sent men to summon surrender; Ji loosed crossbows and shot at them.
translations.idiomatic: Arighaiya sent envoys offering terms; Ji answered with crossbow fire.

sentences.zh: 攻三月，塈夜不解甲，前後百餘戰，城中死傷相籍，訖無降意。

translations.literal: The siege lasted three months. Ji did not remove his armor at night; there were more than a hundred battles before and after; within the city the dead and wounded lay piled upon one another, yet to the end there was no thought of surrender.
translations.idiomatic: For three months Ji never took off his armor. He fought more than a hundred engagements; corpses and wounded filled the streets, yet he never wavered.

sentences.zh: 城東隅稍卑，大軍陽攻西門，以精兵夜決水閘，攻東門，破其外城；

translations.literal: The southeast corner of the wall was somewhat lower. The great army feigned an attack on the west gate, then by night with elite troops opened the sluice gates and attacked the east gate, breaking the outer city.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern corner of the wall was slightly lower. The enemy feigned an assault on the west gate, then by night elite troops breached the sluice and stormed the east gate, taking the outer city.

sentences.zh: 塈閉內城城守，又破之。

translations.literal: Ji shut the inner city and continued to defend; it too was broken.
translations.idiomatic: Ji withdrew into the inner citadel and held on until that too fell.

sentences.zh: 塈率死士巷戰，刀傷臂被執，殺之斷其首，猶握拳奮起，立逾時始仆。

translations.literal: Ji led death-loyal soldiers in street fighting; his arm was cut by a blade and he was seized. They killed him and severed his head, yet he still clenched his fist and sprang up, standing for more than a watch before he fell.
translations.idiomatic: Ji led his last loyal men in street fighting until a blade cut his arm and he was seized. They killed him and cut off his head, yet his fist remained clenched and his body stood erect for a long while before it toppled.

sentences.zh: 靜江破，邕守馬成旺及其子都統應麒以城降，獨塈部將婁鈴轄猶以二百五十人守月城不下。

translations.literal: When Jingjiang fell, the Yong prefect Ma Chengwang and his son the commander-in-chief Yingqi surrendered the city; only Ji's subordinate the bell-commander Lou still held the moon city with two hundred fifty men and would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: After Jingjiang fell, Yong's prefect Ma Chengwang and his son Commander Yingqi surrendered, but Ji's subordinate Commander Lou still held the moon citadel with 250 men and refused to submit.

sentences.zh: 阿裏海牙笑曰：“是何足攻。

translations.literal: Arighaiya laughed and said, "What is this worth attacking?"
translations.idiomatic: Arighaiya laughed and said, "What is this rabble worth besieging?"

sentences.zh: ”圍之十餘日，婁從壁上呼曰：“吾屬饑，不能出降，苟賜之食，當聽命。

translations.literal: They besieged it for more than ten days. Lou called from atop the wall, "We are starving and cannot come out to surrender; if you grant us food, we will obey."
translations.idiomatic: They invested it for ten days. Lou shouted from the wall, "We are starving—we cannot march out to surrender. Send us food and we will obey."

sentences.zh: ”乃遺之牛數頭，米數斛。

translations.literal: They then sent him several head of cattle and several hu of rice.
translations.idiomatic: They sent several oxen and a few hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 一部將開門取歸，復閉壁。

translations.literal: One officer opened the gate to fetch them back and again shut the walls.
translations.idiomatic: An officer opened the gate to bring the supplies in, then shut the walls again.

sentences.zh: 大軍乘高視之，兵皆分米，炊未熟，生臠牛，啖立盡。

translations.literal: The great army looked down from high ground; the soldiers all divided the rice, and before it was cooked they cut the oxen raw and ate them standing until all was gone.
translations.idiomatic: Watching from the heights, the besiegers saw the defenders divide the grain; before it was even cooked they butchered the oxen raw and devoured them on the spot.

sentences.zh: 鳴角伐鼓，諸將以為出戰也，甲以待。

translations.literal: Horns sounded and drums beat; the generals thought they were coming out to fight and donned armor to wait.
translations.idiomatic: Horns and drums sounded; the Mongol generals thought a sortie was coming and armored their men to receive it.

sentences.zh: 婁乃令所部入擁一火炮然之，聲如雷霆，震城土皆崩，煙氣漲天外，兵多驚死者。

translations.literal: Lou then ordered his men to crowd in around one cannon and fire it; the sound was like thunder, shaking the city earth until it collapsed, smoke swelling beyond the sky, and many soldiers died of fright.
translations.idiomatic: Lou had his men pack around a single cannon and fire it. The blast was like thunder; the walls crumbled and smoke billowed to the heavens. Many enemy soldiers died of shock alone.

sentences.zh: 火熄入視之，灰燼無遺矣。

translations.literal: When the fire died they entered to look; not even ashes remained.
translations.idiomatic: When the smoke cleared they entered and found nothing left but ash.

sentences.zh: 密佑，其先密州人，後渡淮居廬州。

translations.literal: Mi You—his ancestors were men of Mizhou; later they crossed the Huai and settled in Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Mi You's family originally came from Mizhou and later crossed the Huai to settle in Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 佑為人剛毅質直，累官至廬州駐劄、御前遊擊中軍統領，改權江西路副總管。

translations.literal: You was by nature firm, resolute, and plain-spoken. He rose through offices to garrison commander at Luzhou and commander of the Imperial Front Mobile Central Army, then was changed to acting deputy overall commander of Jiangxi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: You was stern, upright, and plain-spoken. He rose to command the Luzhou garrison and the Imperial Front Mobile Central Army, then became acting deputy overall commander of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 鹹淳十年，以閣門宣讚舍人為江西都統。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xianchun he was made overall commander of Jiangxi as Gate Attendant and Proclamation Aide.
translations.idiomatic: In 1274 he was appointed overall commander of Jiangxi with the title Gate Attendant and Proclamation Aide.

sentences.zh: 是冬，大元丞相伯顏下鄂州，留右丞阿裏海牙守之，而將大兵東下。

translations.literal: That winter the Great Yuan Chancellor Bayan took E Prefecture, left the Right Chancellor Arighaiya to guard it, and led the great army eastward.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the Yuan Chancellor Bayan took Ezhou, left Arighaiya to hold it, and marched his main force east.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，朱礻巽孫遣高世傑取鄂州，阿裏海牙以兵逆擊，執世傑荊江口，兵盡潰，半入江西。

translations.literal: In the second month of the next year Zhu Sunsun sent Gao Shijie to take E Prefecture. Arighaiya met him with troops, seized Shijie at the Jing River mouth, the army wholly collapsed, and half fled into Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: The following February Zhu Sunsun sent Gao Shijie to retake Ezhou. Arighaiya met him, captured Shijie at the Jing River mouth, and routed the army; half the survivors fled into Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 江西製置黃萬石招集之，且募寧都、廣昌、南劍義兵千餘人，盡以屬佑。

translations.literal: Jiangxi Pacification Commissioner Huang Wanshi gathered them in and also recruited more than a thousand righteous militia from Ningdu, Guangchang, and Nanjian, placing them all under You.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi Pacification Commissioner Huang Wanshi gathered the refugees and raised more than a thousand militia from Ningdu, Guangchang, and Nanjian, placing them all under You's command.

sentences.zh: 十一月，大兵至隆興，劉槃兵敗，乃嬰城自守。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the great army reached Longxing. Liu Pan's army was defeated and he then clung to the city in self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the enemy reached Longxing. Liu Pan was defeated and shut himself inside the city.

sentences.zh: 萬石時移治撫州，將遁，懼佑不從，乃調佑兵援槃，且戒以勿戰。

translations.literal: Wanshi had then moved his administration to Fuzhou and was about to flee; fearing You would not follow, he transferred You's troops to relieve Pan and moreover warned him not to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Wanshi had moved his headquarters to Fuzhou and planned to flee. Fearing You would refuse to abandon the fight, he ordered You's troops to relieve Liu Pan but warned him not to engage the enemy.

sentences.zh: 未至隆興，槃已降，都統夏驥率所部兵潰圍出。

translations.literal: Before reaching Longxing, Pan had already surrendered. The commander-in-chief Xia Ji led his own troops in breaking out of the encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: Before You arrived, Liu Pan had already surrendered. Commander Xia Ji broke out of the encirclement with his own troops.

sentences.zh: 已而元帥張榮實、呂師夔提兵逼撫州，佑率眾逆之進賢坪，兵來呼曰：“降者乎？

translations.literal: Before long the marshals Zhang Rongshi and Lü Shikui led troops to press Fuzhou. You led the multitude to meet them at Jinxianping. The soldiers came calling, "Do you surrender?
translations.idiomatic: Soon the marshals Zhang Rongshi and Lü Shikui advanced on Fuzhou. You met them at Jinxianping. The enemy called out, "Will you surrender?

sentences.zh: 鬥者乎？

translations.literal: Or do you fight?"
translations.idiomatic: Or will you fight?"

sentences.zh: ”佑曰：“鬥者也。

translations.literal: You said, "We fight."
translations.idiomatic: You answered, "We fight."

sentences.zh: ”麾其兵突戰，進至龍馬坪，大兵圍之數重，矢下如雨。

translations.literal: He waved his troops into sudden battle and advanced to Longmaping. The great army surrounded them in many rings; arrows fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: He led a charge to Longmaping, where the enemy surrounded them layer upon layer and arrows fell like rain.

sentences.zh: 佑告其部曰：“今日死日也，若力戰，或有生理。

translations.literal: You told his troops, "Today is the day to die; if we fight with force, there may yet be a way to live."
translations.idiomatic: You told his men, "Today we die—but if we fight with all our strength, we may yet live."

sentences.zh: ”眾鹹憤厲。

translations.literal: The multitude all burned with indignant fury.
translations.idiomatic: They burned with righteous fury.

sentences.zh: 自辰戰至日昃，佑麵中矢，拔之復戰，又身被四矢三槍，眾皆死，僅餘數十人。

translations.literal: From the chen watch they fought until the sun slanted; an arrow struck You in the face, he pulled it out and fought again, and again his body took four arrows and three spear wounds. The multitude all died; only several tens remained.
translations.idiomatic: They fought from morning until afternoon. An arrow struck You in the face; he pulled it out and fought on until four more arrows and three spear wounds had found him. His men fell around him until only a few dozen remained.

sentences.zh: 佑乃揮雙刀斫圍南走，前渡橋，馬踏板斷，遂被執。

translations.literal: You then swung twin blades to hack through the encirclement and fled south; when he reached the bridge ahead, the horse's tread broke the planks and he was seized.
translations.idiomatic: Wielding two swords he hacked his way south through the ring. At the bridge ahead his horse broke through the planks and he was captured.

sentences.zh: 眾見其勇，戒勿殺，輿歸隆興。

translations.literal: The multitude, seeing his valor, warned one another not to kill him and carried him in a litter back to Longxing.
translations.idiomatic: Impressed by his courage, his captors forbade anyone to kill him and carried him in a litter back to Longxing.

sentences.zh: 元帥宋都

translations.literal: The marshal Song Du
translations.idiomatic: Marshal Song Du

translations.literal: Jiaozhu)
translations.idiomatic: Jiaozhu)

sentences.zh: 曰：“壯士也。

translations.literal: said, "A true stalwart."
translations.idiomatic: said, "What a warrior."

sentences.zh: ”欲降之，係之月餘，終不屈。

translations.literal: He wished to win his surrender and bound him for more than a month, yet in the end he would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: He wanted to win him over and kept him bound for more than a month, but You never yielded.

sentences.zh: 嚐罵萬石為賣國小人，使我誌不得伸。

translations.literal: He once cursed Wanshi as a petty man who sold out the state, making it impossible for his own ambition to be fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: He cursed Huang Wanshi as a traitor who had sold out the country and thwarted his own purpose.

sentences.zh: 宋都

translations.literal: Song Du
translations.idiomatic: Song Du

translations.literal: (Jiaozhu)
translations.idiomatic: (Jiaozhu)

sentences.zh: 命劉槃、呂師夔坐城樓，引佑樓下，以金符遺之，許以官，佑不受，語侵槃、師夔，益不遜。

translations.literal: ordered Liu Pan and Lü Shikui to sit on the city tower, led You below the tower, presented him with a gold tally, and promised him office. You would not accept and his words insulted Pan and Shikui, growing ever more insolent.
translations.idiomatic: had Liu Pan and Lü Shikui sit on the city tower, brought You below, offered him a gold tally and an office. You refused and insulted Pan and Shikui ever more brazenly.

sentences.zh: 又令佑子說之曰：“父死，子安之？

translations.literal: He again had You's son persuade him, saying, "When the father dies, where shall the son find peace?"
translations.idiomatic: He then had You's son plead with him: "Father, if you die, what will become of your son?"

sentences.zh: ”佑斥曰：“汝行乞於市，第雲密都統子，誰不憐汝也。

translations.literal: You shouted him down, saying, "Go beg in the market—only say you are the son of Commander Mi Du, and who will not pity you?"
translations.idiomatic: You snapped, "Go beg in the marketplace—just say you are Commander Mi's son, and who will not take pity on you?"

sentences.zh: ”怡然自解其衣請刑，遂死。

translations.literal: Calmly he undid his own garments and asked for execution, and so died.
translations.idiomatic: Calmly he stripped off his own clothes and asked for execution. And so he died.

sentences.zh: 觀者皆泣下。

translations.literal: All who watched wept.
translations.idiomatic: Every witness wept.

sentences.zh: 張世傑，范陽人。

translations.literal: Zhang Shijie was a man of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shijie came from Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 少從張柔戍杞，有罪，遂奔宋，隸淮兵中，無所知名。

translations.literal: In youth he followed Zhang Rou to garrison Qi, committed an offense, and therefore fled to Song, enrolled among the Huai troops, and was unknown to anyone.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he served under Zhang Rou at Qi, committed an offense, fled to the Song side, and joined the Huai army without making a name for himself.

sentences.zh: 阮思聰見而奇之，言之呂文德，文德召為小校。

translations.literal: Ruan Sicong saw him and thought him extraordinary, spoke of him to Lü Wende, and Wende summoned him as a junior officer.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Sicong spotted his talent and recommended him to Lü Wende, who took him on as a junior officer.

sentences.zh: 累功至黃州武定諸軍都統製。

translations.literal: Through accumulated merit he reached commander-in-chief of the Wuding Armies of Huang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Through repeated merit he rose to commander-in-chief of the Wuding armies at Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 攻安東州，戰疾力，與高達援鄂州有功，轉十官。

translations.literal: He attacked Andong Prefecture and fought with fierce exertion; with Gao Da he relieved E Prefecture with merit and was transferred ten ranks.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Andong with furious energy and, with Gao Da, distinguished himself relieving Ezhou, earning ten promotions.

sentences.zh: 尋從賈似道入黃州，戰類草坪，奪還所俘，加環衛官，曆知高郵軍、安東州。

translations.literal: Soon he followed Jia Sidao into Huang Prefecture, fought at Leicao Plain, recovered captives taken, was added as an imperial guard officer, and successively governed Gaoyou Army and Andong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Jia Sidao into Huangzhou, fought at Leicao Plain, recaptured prisoners, was made an imperial guard officer, and served as prefect of Gaoyou and Andong in turn.

sentences.zh: 鹹淳四年，大軍築鹿門堡，呂文德請益兵於朝，調世傑與夏貴赴之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianchun the great army built Lumen Fort. Lü Wende requested reinforcements from court; Shijie and Xia Gui were transferred to go.
translations.idiomatic: In 1268 the Mongols built Lumen Fort. Lü Wende asked court for reinforcements, and Shijie was sent with Xia Gui.

sentences.zh: 及呂文煥以襄陽降，命世傑將五千人守鄂州。

translations.literal: When Lü Wenhuan surrendered Xiangyang, Shijie was ordered to lead five thousand men to defend E Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Wenhuan surrendered Xiangyang, Shijie was ordered to hold Ezhou with five thousand men.

sentences.zh: 世傑以鐵縆鎖兩城，夾以炮弩，其要津皆施杙，設攻具。

translations.literal: Shijie used iron chains to lock the two cities, flanked them with cannon and crossbows, set stakes at every critical ford, and deployed assault equipment.
translations.idiomatic: He chained the twin cities with iron cables, lined them with cannon and crossbows, staked every critical crossing, and prepared every siege device.

sentences.zh: 大軍破新城，長驅而下，世傑力戰，不得前，遣人招之，不聽。

translations.literal: The great army broke Xincheng and drove straight down. Shijie fought with all his strength and they could not advance; they sent men to summon him, but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy took Xincheng and swept downstream. Shijie fought them to a halt; they sent envoys offering terms, but he refused to hear them.

sentences.zh: 丞相伯顏陽攻嚴山隘，潛自唐港蕩舟入漢，東攻鄂，鄂降。

translations.literal: Chancellor Bayan feigned an attack on Yanshan Pass, secretly poled boats from Tang Harbor into the Han, attacked E from the east, and E surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Bayan feigned an assault on Yanshan Pass while secretly sending boats from Tang Harbor into the Han to strike Ezhou from the east. Ezhou fell.

sentences.zh: 世傑提所部兵入衛，道復饒州，乃入朝。

translations.literal: Shijie led his own troops to enter the capital for defense, recovered Rao Prefecture on the way, and then entered court.
translations.idiomatic: Shijie marched his troops to the capital for its defense, recovered Rao Prefecture en route, and presented himself at court.

sentences.zh: 時方危急，征諸將勤王多不至，獨世傑來，上下歎異。

translations.literal: The times were just then critically perilous; generals summoned to aid the throne mostly did not come—only Shijie came, and above and below marveled.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty was in desperate straits; of all the generals summoned to save the throne, only Shijie answered. Court and people alike were astonished.

sentences.zh: 自和州防禦使不數月累加至保康軍承宣使，總都督府兵。

translations.literal: From Defender of He Prefecture, in less than several months he was repeatedly promoted to commissioner of the Baokang Army and took overall command of the Grand Marshal's troops.
translations.idiomatic: Within months he rose from defender of Hezhou to commissioner of the Baokang Army and commander of all forces under the Grand Marshal's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 遣將四出，取浙西諸郡，復平江、安吉、廣德、溧陽諸城，兵勢頗振。

translations.literal: He sent generals out in four directions to take the various prefectures of Zhe West, recovered Pingjiang, Anji, Guangde, Liyang, and other cities, and military momentum revived considerably.
translations.idiomatic: He sent generals in every direction to recover the prefectures of Zhe West—Pingjiang, Anji, Guangde, Liyang, and others—and the Song cause rallied.

sentences.zh: 七月，與劉師勇諸將大出師焦山，令以十舟為方，碇江中，非有號令毋發碇，示以必死。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, with Liu Shiyong and other generals, he launched a great campaign from Jiaoshan, ordering ten boats to form a square, anchor in mid-river, and not weigh anchor without command—showing they would certainly die.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he joined Liu Shiyong and others in a major offensive from Jiaoshan. He arrayed the fleet in squares of ten ships, anchored in midstream, and forbade any vessel to weigh anchor without orders—a pledge to fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 元帥阿術載彀士以火矢攻之，世傑兵亂，無敢發碇，赴江死者萬餘人。

translations.literal: Marshal Azhu loaded ballista soldiers to attack with fire arrows. Shijie's army fell into disorder; none dared weigh anchor, and more than ten thousand who plunged into the river died.
translations.idiomatic: Marshal Azhu attacked with fire arrows from ballista ships. Shijie's fleet panicked; no one dared raise anchor, and more than ten thousand men drowned in the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 大敗，奔圌山。

translations.literal: Greatly defeated, he fled to Mount Chun.
translations.idiomatic: Utterly defeated, he fled to Mount Chun.

sentences.zh: 上疏請濟師，不報。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting relief troops; there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized begging for reinforcements, but court never answered.

sentences.zh: 尋擢龍、神衛四廂都指揮使。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to commander of the four wings of the Dragon and Spirit Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to commander of the four wings of the Dragon and Spirit Guards.

sentences.zh: 十月，進沿江招討使，改製置副使、兼知江陰軍。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he advanced to Yangzi-route pacification commissioner, was changed to vice pacification commissioner, and concurrently governed Jiangyin Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he became Yangzi-route pacification commissioner, vice pacification commissioner, and concurrent prefect of Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 已而大軍至獨鬆關，召文天祥入衛，以世傑為保康軍節度使、知平江。

translations.literal: Before long the great army reached Dusong Pass; Wen Tianxiang was summoned to enter the capital for defense, and Shijie was made military commissioner of the Baokang Army and prefect of Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy reached Dusong Pass, Wen Tianxiang was recalled to the capital and Shijie was made military commissioner of the Baokang Army and prefect of Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 尋亦召入衛，加檢校少保。

translations.literal: Soon he too was summoned to enter the capital for defense and was added as acting Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: He too was soon recalled to the capital and made acting Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，大軍迫臨安，世傑請移三宮入海，而與天祥合兵背城一戰。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year the great army pressed Lin'an. Shijie requested moving the three palaces out to sea and joining Tianxiang to combine forces for one battle with their backs to the wall.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 1276 the enemy closed on Lin'an. Shijie urged sending the imperial family to sea and joining Wen Tianxiang for one last battle with their backs to the city walls.

sentences.zh: 丞相陳宜中方遣人請和，不可，白太皇太后止之。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Chen Yizhong was just then sending men to sue for peace; this could not be allowed, and he informed the Grand Empress Dowager to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Chen Yizhong was already sending envoys to sue for peace. Shijie would not permit it and appealed to the Grand Empress Dowager to stop the negotiations.

sentences.zh: 未幾，和議亦沮。

translations.literal: Before long the peace talks also collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the peace talks collapsed as well.

sentences.zh: 兵至皋亭山，世傑乃提兵入定海。

translations.literal: When troops reached Gaoting Mountain, Shijie then led his army into Dinghai.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy reached Gaoting Mountain, Shijie withdrew his forces to Dinghai.

sentences.zh: 石國英遣都統卞彪說之使降，世傑以為彪來從己俱南也，椎牛享之，酒半，彪從容為言，世傑大怒，斷其舌，磔之巾子山。

translations.literal: Shi Guoying sent the commander-in-chief Bian Biao to persuade him to surrender. Shijie thought Biao had come to follow him south together; he slaughtered an ox to feast him, and when the wine was half gone Biao calmly spoke his message. Shijie was greatly angered, cut out his tongue, and dismembered him on Mount Jinzi.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Guoying sent Commander Bian Biao to offer surrender terms. Shijie thought Biao had come to join him in the south, slaughtered an ox to feast him, but halfway through the banquet Biao broached his mission. Shijie flew into a rage, cut out his tongue, and had him dismembered on Mount Jinzi.

sentences.zh: 四月，從二王入福州。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he followed the two princes into Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he followed the two princes into Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 五月，與宜中奉昰為主，拜簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, with Yizhong, he enthroned Zhao Shi as ruler and was appointed Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he and Chen Yizhong enthroned Zhao Shi and made Shijie Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 王世強導大軍攻之，世傑乃奉益王入海，而自將陳吊眼、許夫人諸畬兵攻蒲壽庚，不下。

translations.literal: Wang Shiqiang guided the great army to attack them. Shijie then escorted Prince Yi to sea, while he personally led Chen Diaoyan, Lady Xu, and the various She militias to attack Pu Shougeng but could not take him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shiqiang guided the Mongol army against them. Shijie put Prince Yi to sea while he personally led Chen Diaoyan, Lady Xu, and the She tribesmen against Pu Shougeng, but could not take Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 十月，元帥唆都將兵來援泉，遂解去。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Marshal Suodu led troops to relieve Quan, and they then lifted the siege and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Marshal Suodu brought reinforcements to Quanzhou and Shijie lifted the siege.

sentences.zh: 既而唆都遣人招益王，又遣經曆孫安甫說世傑，世傑拘安甫軍中不遣。

translations.literal: Before long Suodu sent men to summon Prince Yi, and also sent the clerk Sun Anfu to persuade Shijie; Shijie detained Anfu in the army and would not release him.
translations.idiomatic: Suodu then sent envoys to win over Prince Yi and clerk Sun Anfu to persuade Shijie. Shijie detained Anfu and refused to release him.

sentences.zh: 招討劉深攻淺灣，世傑兵敗，移王居井澳，深復來攻井澳，世傑戰卻之，因徒石碙洲。

translations.literal: Pacification Commissioner Liu Shen attacked Qianwan. Shijie's army was defeated and he moved the king's residence to Jing'ao. Shen again came to attack Jing'ao; Shijie fought him off and therefore moved to Shiqiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shen attacked Qianwan. Shijie was defeated and moved the court to Jing'ao. When Liu Shen attacked again, Shijie drove him off and relocated to Shiqiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 至元十五年正月，遣將王用攻雷州，用敗績。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifteenth year of Zhiyuan he sent the general Wang Yong to attack Lei Prefecture; Yong was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 1278 he sent General Wang Yong against Leizhou; Yong was defeated.

sentences.zh: 四月，益王殂，衛王昺立，拜世傑少傅、樞密副使。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Prince Yi died; Prince Wei Zhao Bing was enthroned, and Shijie was appointed Junior Tutor and Vice Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Prince Yi died and Prince Wei Zhao Bing succeeded him. Shijie was made Junior Tutor and Vice Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 五月，遣瓊州安撫張應科攻雷州，三戰皆不利。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he sent the Leizhou pacification commissioner Zhang Yingke to attack Lei Prefecture; three battles were all unfavorable.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he sent Zhang Yingke, pacification commissioner of Qiongzhou, against Leizhou; three battles went against them.

sentences.zh: 六月，再決戰雷城下，應科死之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month they fought again decisively below Lei city; Yingke died in it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month they fought again before Leizhou; Zhang Yingke was killed.

sentences.zh: 世傑以碙洲不可居，徙王新會之崖山。

translations.literal: Shijie, because Shiqiaozhou could not be dwelt in, moved the king to Yamen in Xinhui.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Shiqiaozhou untenable, Shijie moved the court to Yamen off the coast of Xinhui.

sentences.zh: 八月，封越國公。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he was enfeoffed as Duke of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he was enfeoffed as Duke of Yue.

sentences.zh: 發瓊州粟以給軍。

translations.literal: He released grain from Qiong Prefecture to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: He drew grain from Qiongzhou to feed the army.

sentences.zh: 十月，遣淩震、王道夫襲廣州，震敗績。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he sent Ling Zhen and Wang Daofu to raid Guangzhou; Zhen was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he sent Ling Zhen and Wang Daofu to strike Guangzhou; Zhen was beaten.

sentences.zh: 明年，元帥張弘範等兵至崖山，或謂世傑曰：“北兵以舟師塞海口，則我不能進退，盍先據海口。

translations.literal: The next year Marshal Zhang Hongfan and others reached Yamen. Some said to Shijie, "If the northern troops block the estuary with their fleet, we cannot advance or retreat—why not seize the estuary first?
translations.idiomatic: The following year Marshal Zhang Hongfan reached Yamen. Some urged Shijie, "If the Mongols seal the estuary with their fleet, we will have no escape—seize the mouth of the bay first.

sentences.zh: 幸而勝，國之福也；

translations.literal: If by fortune we win, it is the state's blessing;
translations.idiomatic: If we win, the dynasty is saved;

sentences.zh: 不勝，猶可西走。

translations.literal: if we do not win, we can still flee west."
translations.idiomatic: if we lose, we can still flee west."

sentences.zh: ”世傑恐久在海上有離心，動則必散，乃曰：“頻年航海，何時已乎？

translations.literal: Shijie feared that long at sea hearts would stray and that once they moved they would surely scatter, and said, "Year after year at sea—when will it end?
translations.idiomatic: Shijie feared that prolonged life at sea would breed disloyalty and that any move would scatter the fleet. He said, "How many more years must we wander the sea?

sentences.zh: 今須與決勝負。

translations.literal: Now we must settle victory and defeat with them."
translations.idiomatic: Now we must settle this once and for all."

sentences.zh: ”悉焚行朝草市，結大舶千餘作水砦，為死守計，人皆危之。

translations.literal: He burned all the traveling court's market sheds, joined more than a thousand great ships into a water fortress, and planned to defend to the death; everyone regarded it as perilous.
translations.idiomatic: He burned the court's shore market, chained more than a thousand great ships into a floating fortress, and resolved to fight to the death. All who saw it were appalled.

sentences.zh: 已而弘範兵至，據海口，樵汲道絕，兵茹幹糧十餘日，渴甚，下掬海水飲之，海鹹，飲即嘔泄，兵大困。

translations.literal: Before long Hongfan's troops arrived and held the estuary; paths for fuel and water were cut off. The soldiers ate dry grain for more than ten days, were desperately thirsty, went down to scoop seawater to drink—it was brine, and drinking at once brought vomiting and diarrhea; the army was greatly distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Hongfan seized the estuary and cut off firewood and fresh water. For more than ten days the men ate only dry rations. Driven mad with thirst, they drank seawater and vomited until the army was near collapse.

sentences.zh: 世傑率蘇劉義、方興日大戰。

translations.literal: Shijie led Su Liu Yi and Fang Xingri in great battles.
translations.idiomatic: Shijie led Su Liu Yi and Fang Xingri in repeated fierce battles.

sentences.zh: 弘範得世傑甥韓，命以官，使三至招之，世傑曆數古忠臣曰：“吾知降，生且富貴，但為主死不移耳。

translations.literal: Hongfan obtained Shijie's nephew Han, gave him office, and sent him three times to summon Shijie. Shijie recounted ancient loyal ministers and said, "I know that if I surrender I shall live in wealth and honor, but to die for my lord without shifting is all."
translations.idiomatic: Hongfan captured Shijie's nephew Han, gave him an office, and sent him three times to win Shijie over. Shijie named the loyal ministers of old and said, "I know surrender would bring me wealth and rank—but I will die for my lord without wavering."

sentences.zh: ”二月癸未，弘範等攻崖山，世傑敗，走衛王舟。

translations.literal: On the day guiwei of the second month Hongfan and others attacked Yamen. Shijie was defeated and fled to Prince Wei's boat.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei day of the second month Hongfan attacked Yamen. Shijie was beaten and fled to Prince Wei's ship.

sentences.zh: 大軍薄中軍，世傑乃斷維，以十餘艦奪港去。

translations.literal: The great army pressed the central fleet; Shijie then cut the cables and with more than ten ships seized the channel and left.
translations.idiomatic: As the enemy closed on the central squadron, Shijie cut his cables and broke through the channel with a dozen ships.

sentences.zh: 後還收兵崖山，劉自立擊敗之，降其將方遇龍、葉秀榮、章文秀等四十餘人。

translations.literal: Later he returned to gather troops at Yamen; Liu Zili defeated him and accepted the surrender of his generals Fang Yulong, Ye Xiurong, Zhang Wenxiu, and more than forty others.
translations.idiomatic: He returned later to rally the remnants at Yamen, but Liu Zili defeated him and accepted the surrender of more than forty of his generals, including Fang Yulong, Ye Xiurong, and Zhang Wenxiu.

sentences.zh: 世傑復欲奉楊太妃求趙氏後而立之，俄颶風壞舟，溺死平章山下。

translations.literal: Shijie again wished to support Grand Consort Yang in seeking a Zhao descendant to enthrone, but soon a typhoon wrecked the boats and he drowned below Mount Pingzhang.
translations.idiomatic: He still hoped to place a Zhao heir on the throne under Grand Consort Yang's protection, but a typhoon wrecked his fleet and he drowned off Mount Pingzhang.

sentences.zh: 劉師勇者，廬州人。

translations.literal: Liu Shiyong was a man of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shiyong came from Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 以戰功曆環衛官。

translations.literal: Through battle merit he rose through imperial guard offices.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the imperial guard ranks on battlefield merit.

sentences.zh: 魯港師潰，賈似道欲東入海，師勇讚之入揚州圖再舉，似道然之。

translations.literal: When the army collapsed at Lugang, Jia Sidao wished to go east onto the sea. Shiyong praised entering Yangzhou to plan another rising, and Sidao agreed.
translations.idiomatic: After the rout at Lugang, Jia Sidao wanted to flee east by sea. Shiyong urged him instead to enter Yangzhou and plan a comeback, and Sidao agreed.

sentences.zh: 時姚訔復常州，似道命師勇以淮兵取呂城，朝廷加師勇和州防禦使，助訔守常，而以張彥守呂城，合兵拒大軍。

translations.literal: At the time Yao Yin recovered Chang Prefecture. Sidao ordered Shiyong to take Lü City with Huai troops. The court added Shiyong as Defender of He Prefecture to help Yin defend Chang, while Zhang Yan held Lü City; they combined forces to resist the great army.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yin had retaken Changzhou. Sidao ordered Shiyong to seize Lücheng with Huai troops. The court made Shiyong defender of Hezhou to help Yin hold Changzhou while Zhang Yan held Lücheng; together they faced the Mongol army.

sentences.zh: 戰失利，彥馬弱，陷淖中見執，呂城失守，常州勢益孤。

translations.literal: The battle went badly; Yan's horses were weak, he sank in the mire and was seized, Lü City was lost, and Chang Prefecture's position grew more isolated.
translations.idiomatic: They were defeated; Yan's horses foundered in the mud and he was captured. Lücheng fell and Changzhou was left utterly isolated.

sentences.zh: 大軍置彥城下招降，師勇以大義斥彥，彥慚而退。

translations.literal: The great army placed Yan below the walls to summon surrender. Shiyong rebuked Yan with righteous principle; Yan withdrew in shame.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy placed Yan before the walls to urge surrender. Shiyong denounced him on grounds of loyalty; Yan withdrew in shame.

sentences.zh: 又遣範文虎來諭，師勇伏弩射走之。

translations.literal: They again sent Fan Wenhu to announce terms; Shiyong set crossbows in ambush and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Wenhu was sent again with offers of peace; Shiyong ambushed him with crossbows and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 常受圍數月，援兵絕，有群鴟飛鳴繞城，眾惡為不祥，俄而城陷。

translations.literal: Chang was besieged for several months and relief troops were cut off. A flock of kites flew crying around the walls; the multitude regarded it as ill-omened, and before long the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhou was besieged for months without relief. Kites circled the walls shrieking—a sign the defenders took for doom—and soon the city fell.

sentences.zh: 師勇拔柵，戰且行，其弟馬墮塹，躍不能出，師勇舉手與訣而去。

translations.literal: Shiyong pulled up the palisade and fought while retreating. His younger brother's horse fell into a ditch; he could not leap out. Shiyong raised his hand in farewell and left.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyong tore down the palisade and fought his way out. His brother's horse fell into a ditch and could not rise; Shiyong raised his hand in farewell and rode on.

sentences.zh: 淮軍數千人皆鬥死。

translations.literal: Several thousand Huai troops all fought to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand Huai soldiers fought to the last man.

sentences.zh: 有婦人伏積屍下，窺淮兵六人反背相拄，殺敵十百人乃殪。

translations.literal: One woman hid beneath piled corpses and watched six Huai soldiers bracing one another back to back, killing a hundred or more of the enemy before they perished.
translations.idiomatic: One woman hid under the heaped dead and saw six Huai soldiers stand back to back, killing a hundred enemies before they themselves fell.

sentences.zh: 師勇從二王至海上，見時事不可為，憂憤縱酒卒，葬於鼓山。

translations.literal: Shiyong followed the two princes to the sea, saw that the times could not be remedied, died from worry and rage while drinking freely, and was buried on Mount Gu.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the two princes to sea, saw the cause was hopeless, drank himself to death in grief and rage, and was buried on Mount Gu.

sentences.zh: 秀夫才思清麗，一時文人少能及之。

translations.literal: Xiufu's talent and thought were clear and refined; few literati of the time could match him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xiufu's prose was lucid and elegant; few scholars of his day could match it.

sentences.zh: 性沉靜，不苟求人知，每僚吏至閣，賓主交歡，秀夫獨斂焉無一語。

translations.literal: By nature he was calm and quiet and did not casually seek others' notice. Whenever subordinate officials came to the bureau, host and guests would exchange pleasantries while Xiufu alone remained withdrawn without a single word.
translations.idiomatic: He was reserved by nature and never courted attention. When colleagues visited the bureau and chatter filled the room, Xiufu alone sat in silence.

sentences.zh: 或時宴集府中，坐尊俎間，矜莊終日，未嚐少有希合。

translations.literal: Sometimes at banquets in the prefectural residence he would sit among the wine vessels, stern and dignified all day, never once showing slight inclination to please.
translations.idiomatic: At feasts in the prefect's hall he would sit among the wine cups, grave and formal all day, never playing to the crowd.

sentences.zh: 至察其事，皆治，庭芝益器之，雖改官不使去己，就幕三遷至主管機宜文字。

translations.literal: When he examined affairs, all were well governed. Tingzhi valued him all the more; though his office was changed he would not let him leave his side. In the secretariat he was promoted three times to director of confidential documents.
translations.idiomatic: Yet everything he handled was in order. Li Tingzhi prized him all the more and, though his title changed, would not let him leave his staff. On the secretariat he rose three times to director of confidential documents.

sentences.zh: 鹹淳十年，庭芝製置淮東，擢參議官。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xianchun Tingzhi was made pacification commissioner of Huai East and promoted Xiufu to deliberation officer.
translations.idiomatic: In 1274 Li Tingzhi became pacification commissioner of Huai East and made Xiufu his deliberation officer.

sentences.zh: 德祐元年，邊事急，諸僚屬多亡者，惟秀夫數人不去。

translations.literal: In the first year of Deyou frontier affairs were urgent; many subordinates fled, but only Xiufu and a few others did not leave.
translations.idiomatic: In 1275 the frontier crisis deepened and most staff fled; only Xiufu and a handful stayed.

sentences.zh: 庭芝上其名，除司農寺丞，累擢至宗正少卿兼權起居舍人。

translations.literal: Tingzhi submitted his name; he was appointed vice director of the Court of the Imperial Clan and through repeated promotions reached Vice Minister of the Imperial Clan and acting Recorder of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi recommended him to court. He was made vice director of the Court of the Imperial Clan and eventually rose to vice minister of that court and acting Recorder of the Left.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，以禮部侍郎使軍前請和，不就而反。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year, as Vice Minister of Rites he was sent to the army front to sue for peace; he did not succeed and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 1276 he went as Vice Minister of Rites to sue for peace at the enemy camp, failed, and returned.

sentences.zh: 二王走溫州，秀夫與蘇劉義追從之，使人召陳宜中、張世傑等皆至，遂相與立益王於福州。

translations.literal: The two princes fled to Wenzhou. Xiufu and Su Liu Yi pursued and followed them, sent men to summon Chen Yizhong, Zhang Shijie, and others—all came—and together they enthroned Prince Yi at Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The two princes fled to Wenzhou. Xiufu and Su Liu Yi followed, summoned Chen Yizhong, Zhang Shijie, and the rest, and together enthroned Prince Yi at Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 進端明殿學士、簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: He advanced to Academician of the Duanming Hall and Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Academician of the Duanming Hall and Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 宜中以秀夫久在兵間，知軍務，每事谘訪始行，秀夫亦悉心讚之，無不自盡。
