translations.literal: Yizhong, because Xiufu had long been among the troops and knew military affairs, consulted him on every matter before acting. Xiufu also devoted his heart to assisting, never failing to give his utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xiufu knew military affairs from long service in the field, Yizhong consulted him on every decision. Xiufu gave his counsel without reserve.

sentences.zh: 旋與議宜中不合，宜中使言者劾罷之。

translations.literal: Soon he disagreed with Yizhong in council. Yizhong had remonstrators impeach and dismiss him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he clashed with Yizhong in council, and Yizhong had censors impeach him out of office.

sentences.zh: 張世傑讓宜中曰：“此何如時，動以台諫論人？

translations.literal: Zhang Shijie reproached Yizhong, saying, "What sort of time is this, that you constantly use censor-remonstrators to attack people?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shijie rebuked him: "What sort of moment is this to be using censors as political weapons?"

sentences.zh: ”宜中皇恐，亟召秀夫還。

translations.literal: Yizhong was terrified and hastily recalled Xiufu.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhong was terrified and hastily recalled Xiufu.

sentences.zh: 時君臣播越海濱，庶事疏略，楊太妃垂簾，與群臣語猶自稱奴。

translations.literal: At the time sovereign and ministers were driven along the seashore; common affairs were neglected. Grand Consort Yang held the curtain and, speaking with the ministers, still called herself "your slave."
translations.idiomatic: Court and emperor were adrift along the coast, government in disarray. Grand Consort Yang held the curtain and still addressed the ministers as "this slave."

sentences.zh: 每時節朝會，秀夫儼然正笏立，如治朝，或時在行中，淒然泣下，以朝衣拭淚，衣盡浥，左右無不悲動者。

translations.literal: At each seasonal court assembly Xiufu would stand upright with tablet in hand as at a well-ordered court; sometimes amid the procession he would weep mournfully, wipe his tears with his court robe until the garment was soaked through, and none at hand failed to be moved to grief.
translations.idiomatic: At each seasonal audience Xiufu stood with tablet in hand as though the court still ruled from Lin'an. Sometimes in the imperial procession he wept until his court robes were soaked, and all who saw it were overcome.

sentences.zh: 屬井澳風，王以驚疾殂，群臣皆欲散去。

translations.literal: When a storm struck Jing'ao the king died of fright-induced illness and the ministers all wished to scatter.
translations.idiomatic: When a storm struck Jing'ao the young emperor died of fright and the ministers wanted to disperse.

sentences.zh: 秀夫曰：“度宗皇帝一子尚在，將焉置之？

translations.literal: Xiufu said, "Emperor Duzong still has one son living—where else shall we place our hopes?
translations.idiomatic: Xiufu said, "Emperor Duzong still has a living son—where else shall we place our hopes?

sentences.zh: 古人有以一旅一成中興者，今百官有司皆具，士卒數萬，天若未欲絕宋，此豈不可為國邪？

translations.literal: The ancients restored the state with a single regiment—now all officials and offices are present and soldiers number in the tens of thousands. If Heaven has not yet wished to end Song, how can this not still be made a state?"
translations.idiomatic: The ancients restored fallen dynasties with a single regiment. We still have the full bureaucracy and tens of thousands of soldiers. If Heaven has not yet abandoned Song, how can we not still make a nation of this?"

sentences.zh: ”乃與眾共立衛王。

translations.literal: Thereupon together with the multitude they enthroned Prince Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Together they enthroned Prince Wei.

sentences.zh: 時陳宜中往占城，以與世傑不協，屢召不至。

translations.literal: At the time Chen Yizhong had gone to Champa; because he did not get along with Shijie, though summoned repeatedly he did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yizhong had gone to Champa and, at odds with Shijie, ignored repeated summonses.

sentences.zh: 乃以秀夫為左丞相，與世傑共秉政。

translations.literal: Xiufu was therefore made Left Chancellor and shared government with Shijie.
translations.idiomatic: Xiufu was made Left Chancellor and shared power with Shijie.

sentences.zh: 時世傑駐兵崖山，秀夫外籌軍旅，內調工役，凡有所述作，又盡出其手。

translations.literal: At the time Shijie stationed troops at Yamen; Xiufu planned armies abroad and regulated labor within, and whatever compositions were needed all came from his hand alone.
translations.idiomatic: While Shijie held Yamen, Xiufu directed military affairs abroad and labor within; every document the court needed passed through his hand alone.

sentences.zh: 雖匆遽流離中，猶日書《大學章句》以勸講。

translations.literal: Though in hurried flight and exile, he still daily wrote the chapter-and-verse commentary on the Great Learning to encourage lecturing.
translations.idiomatic: Even in frantic flight he copied out the Great Learning day by day to encourage study.

sentences.zh: 至元十六年二月，崖山破，秀夫走衛王舟，而世傑、劉義各斷維去，秀夫度不可脫，乃杖劍驅妻子入海，即負王赴海死，年四十四。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixteenth year of Zhiyuan Yamen fell. Xiufu ran to Prince Wei's boat, while Shijie and Liu Yi each cut their cables and left. Xiufu judged that escape was impossible, took up his staff-sword to drive wife and children into the sea, then bore the king on his back into the sea and died. He was forty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of 1279 Yamen fell. Xiufu reached Prince Wei's ship, but Shijie and Liu Yi had already cut loose and fled. Seeing no escape, he drove his wife and children into the sea with his sword, then carried the boy emperor on his back into the waves. He was forty-four.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士劉鼎孫亦驅家屬並輜重沉海，不死被執，搒掠無完膚，一夕得脫，卒蹈海。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Liu Dingsun also drove his household and baggage into the sea. Not dying, he was seized, beaten until no patch of skin was whole, escaped one night, and finally drowned himself in the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Liu Dingsun drove his family and baggage into the sea. He survived capture and beating until no inch of skin was whole, escaped one night, and finally drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 鼎孫字伯鎮，江陵人，進士也。

translations.literal: Dingsun, courtesy name Bozhen, was a man of Jiangling and a presented scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dingsun, courtesy name Bozhen, was a presented scholar from Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 方秀夫海上時，記二王事為一書甚悉，以授禮部侍郎鄧光薦曰：“君後死，幸傳之。

translations.literal: While Xiufu was at sea he recorded the affairs of the two princes in one book, very detailed, and gave it to Vice Minister of Rites Deng Guangjian, saying, "You will die after me—please transmit it."
translations.idiomatic: While at sea Xiufu compiled a detailed record of the two princes' reign and gave it to Vice Minister of Rites Deng Guangjian, saying, "You will outlive me—see that it survives."

sentences.zh: ”其後崖山平，光薦以其書還廬陵。

translations.literal: Afterward, when Yamen was pacified, Guangjian returned the book to Luling.
translations.idiomatic: After Yamen fell, Guangjian took the manuscript back to Luling.

sentences.zh: 大德初，光薦卒，其書存亡無從知，故海上之事，世莫得其詳雲。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dade era Guangjian died; whether the book survived cannot be known, and therefore affairs at sea—the world has not obtained their full detail.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dade era Guangjian died, and whether the book survived is unknown. That is why the world knows so little of what happened at sea.

sentences.zh: 徐應鑣，字巨翁，衢之江山人，世為衢望族。

translations.literal: Xu Yingbiao, courtesy name Juweng, was a man of Jiangshan in Qu Prefecture; for generations his family was a leading clan of Qu.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yingbiao, whose courtesy name was Juweng, came from Jiangshan in Qu Prefecture. His family had for generations been one of the leading clans of the region.

sentences.zh: 鹹淳末，試補太學生。

translations.literal: At the end of the Xianchun era he tested and was enrolled as a student of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Xianchun reign he entered the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 德祐二年，宋亡，瀛國公入燕，三學生百餘人皆從行。

translations.literal: In the second year of Deyou Song perished; the Duke of Ying entered Yan, and more than a hundred students of the Three Academies all followed on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: In 1276 the Song fell. The young Emperor Gong was taken to Yan, and more than a hundred university students were ordered to accompany him north.

sentences.zh: 應鑣不欲從，乃與其子琦、崧、女元娘誓共焚，子女皆喜從之。

translations.literal: Yingbiao did not wish to follow and therefore with his sons Qi and Song and his daughter Yuanniang swore to burn themselves together; the sons and daughter were all glad to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Yingbiao refused to go. He swore with his sons Qi and Song and his daughter Yuanniang to die by fire together, and they gladly agreed.

sentences.zh: 太學故岳飛第，有飛祠，應鑣具酒肉祀飛曰：“天不祐宋，社稷為墟，應鑣死以報國，誓不與諸生俱北。

translations.literal: The Imperial University was formerly Yue Fei's residence and had a shrine to Yue. Yingbiao set out wine and meat to sacrifice to Yue, saying, "Heaven does not bless Song; the altars of state lie in ruins. Yingbiao dies to repay the state and swears not to go north with the other students."
translations.idiomatic: The university occupied Yue Fei's old residence, where his shrine still stood. Yingbiao offered wine and meat before the general's image and said, "Heaven has abandoned Song and the altars lie in ruins. I die to repay my country and swear I will not go north with the other students."

sentences.zh: 死已，將魂魄累王，作配神主，與王英靈，永永無斁。

translations.literal: After death I shall attach my soul to the Prince, make a spirit tablet as his companion deity, and with the Prince's heroic spirit remain forever without end."
translations.idiomatic: After death my soul shall attend the Prince as a companion spirit, sharing his heroic presence forever."

sentences.zh: ” 琦亦賦詩以自誓。

translations.literal: Qi also composed a poem to bind himself by oath.
translations.idiomatic: Qi too wrote a poem pledging himself to the same end.

sentences.zh: 祭畢，以酒肉餉諸仆，諸仆醉臥，應鑣乃與其子女入梯雲樓，積諸房書籍箱笥四周，縱火自焚。

translations.literal: When the sacrifice was finished he gave wine and meat to the servants; the servants drank themselves drunk and lay down. Yingbiao then entered the Ladder-to-Clouds Tower with his sons and daughter, piled books, boxes, and chests from the rooms all around, and set fire to burn himself.
translations.idiomatic: After the rites he feasted the servants until they lay drunk. Then he and his children entered the Ladder-to-Clouds Tower, heaped books and chests around them, and set the fire.

sentences.zh: 一小仆未寐，聞火聲，起至樓下穴牖視之，應鑣父子儼然坐立，如廟塑像。

translations.literal: One young servant had not slept; hearing the sound of fire he rose, went below the tower, and peered through a hole in the window. Yingbiao and his sons sat upright as if temple statues.
translations.idiomatic: A young servant who had not drunk heard the flames, looked through a crack in the wall, and saw Yingbiao and his children sitting upright like temple images.

sentences.zh: 走報諸仆，壞壁入，撲滅火。

translations.literal: He ran to tell the other servants; they broke through the wall, entered, and beat out the fire.
translations.idiomatic: He roused the others; they broke through the wall and extinguished the blaze.

sentences.zh: 應鑣不得死，與其子女怏怏出戶去，倉卒莫知所之，翌日得其屍祠前井中，皆僵立瞠目，麵如生。

translations.literal: Yingbiao could not die; displeased, he went out the door with his sons and daughter. In haste no one knew where they had gone. The next day their corpses were found in the well before the shrine, all stiffly standing with eyes wide open, faces as in life.
translations.idiomatic: Yingbiao failed to die. He left with his children in bitter disappointment. The next day their bodies were found in the shrine well, standing rigid with eyes wide open, faces unchanged in death.

sentences.zh: 諸仆為具棺斂，殯之西湖金牛僧舍。

translations.literal: The servants prepared coffins and burial rites and interred them at the Golden Ox monk's lodge west of the lake.
translations.idiomatic: The servants coffined them and laid them to rest at the Golden Ox monastery west of West Lake.

sentences.zh: 益王立福州，褒其節，贈朝奉郎、秘閣修撰。

translations.literal: When Prince Yi was enthroned at Fuzhou his integrity was praised and he was posthumously given Court Gentleman for Attendance and Compiler at the Secretariat Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yi was enthroned at Fuzhou, court honored his integrity with the posthumous titles Court Gentleman for Attendance and Compiler at the Secretariat Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 後十年，其同舍生劉汝鈞率儒者五十餘人收而葬之方家峪，私諡曰正節先生。

translations.literal: Ten years later his fellow student Liu Rujun led more than fifty scholars to gather and bury them at Fangjiayu, privately posthumously titling him Master of Upright Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years later his classmate Liu Rujun led more than fifty scholars to reinter them at Fangjiayu and gave him the private posthumous title Master of Upright Integrity.

sentences.zh: 陳文龍字君賁，福州興化人。

translations.literal: Chen Wenlong, courtesy name Junbin, was a man of Xinghua in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wenlong, whose courtesy name was Junbin, came from Xinghua in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 丞相俊卿之後也。

translations.literal: He was a descendant of Chief Minister Junqing.
translations.idiomatic: He was descended from Chief Minister Chen Junqing.

sentences.zh: 能文章，負氣節。

translations.literal: He was capable in literary composition and bore firm moral integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He was a gifted writer and a man of fierce integrity.

sentences.zh: 初名子龍，鹹淳五年廷對第一，度宗易其名文龍。

translations.literal: His original name was Zilong. In the fifth year of Xianchun he ranked first in the palace examination; Emperor Duzong changed his name to Wenlong.
translations.idiomatic: Originally named Zilong, he ranked first in the palace examination of 1269; Emperor Duzong renamed him Wenlong.

sentences.zh: 丞相賈似道愛其文，雅禮重之。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Jia Sidao loved his writing and treated him with refined courtesy and respect.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Jia Sidao admired his writing and treated him with marked respect.

sentences.zh: 由鎮東軍節度判官、曆崇政殿說書、秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: From judge of the Zhendong Army he rose through Lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall and Proofreader of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from judge of the Zhendong Army through lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall to proofreader of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 數年，拜監察御史，皆出似道力。

translations.literal: After several years he was appointed Investigating Censor, all through Sidao's power.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years he was made investigating censor, entirely through Sidao's patronage.

sentences.zh: 然自十數年，似道所置台諫皆闒茸，台中相承，凡有所建白，皆呈稿似道始行。

translations.literal: Yet for more than ten years the censors and remonstrators Sidao appointed were all incompetent; within the bureau it was handed down that whatever memorials were submitted must be shown in draft to Sidao before they could be issued.
translations.idiomatic: For more than a decade Sidao had packed the censorate with mediocrities. By custom every memorial had to be shown to Sidao in draft before it could be issued.

sentences.zh: 至文龍為之，獨不呈稿，已忤似道。

translations.literal: When Wenlong held the post he alone did not present drafts and had already offended Sidao.
translations.idiomatic: Wenlong alone refused to show drafts in advance—and had already offended Sidao.

sentences.zh: 知臨安府洪起畏請行類田，似道主其說，文龍上疏以為不可，似道怒，寢其疏。

translations.literal: The Lin'an prefect Hong Qiwei requested implementing categorized fields; Sidao championed the proposal. Wenlong memorialized that it could not be done; Sidao was angry and shelved his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Lin'an Prefect Hong Qiwei proposed a categorized-field tax scheme that Sidao favored. Wenlong memorialized against it; Sidao was furious and suppressed the memorial.

sentences.zh: 襄陽久被圍，似道日恣淫樂，不少加意，時陽請督師，而陰使其黨留己，竟失襄陽。

translations.literal: Xiangyang had long been besieged, yet Sidao daily indulged in lewd pleasure without the slightest attention. He openly requested to supervise the army while secretly having his faction keep him in place, and in the end Xiangyang was lost.
translations.idiomatic: While Xiangyang starved under siege, Sidao gave himself to pleasure. He publicly asked to take command while secretly arranging to stay put—and Xiangyang fell.

sentences.zh: 文龍上疏極言其失。

translations.literal: Wenlong memorialized vehemently enumerating his failures.
translations.idiomatic: Wenlong memorialized in blistering detail listing his failures.

sentences.zh: 範文虎總師無功，似道芘之，以知安慶，又除趙溍知建康，黃萬石知臨安。

translations.literal: Fan Wenhu commanded the army without achievement; Sidao shielded him and made him prefect of Anqing. Zhao Jin was also appointed prefect of Jiankang and Huang Wanshi prefect of Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Wenhu had failed as commander-in-chief, yet Sidao protected him and made him prefect of Anqing. Zhao Jin was made prefect of Jiankang and Huang Wanshi prefect of Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 文龍言：“文虎失襄陽，今反見擢用，是當罰而賞也。

translations.literal: Wenlong said, "Wenhu lost Xiangyang and now is instead promoted and employed—this is punishing when one should reward."
translations.idiomatic: Wenlong said, "Wenhu lost Xiangyang and is now rewarded—that is to punish merit and reward failure."

sentences.zh: 溍乳臭小子，何以任大閫之寄？

translations.literal: Jin is a milk-smelling stripling—how can he bear the charge of a great command?"
translations.idiomatic: Jin is a callow boy—how can he hold a frontier command?"

sentences.zh: 萬石政事怠荒，以為京尹，何以能治？

translations.literal: Wanshi's administration is slack and negligent—making him capital prefect, how can he govern?"
translations.idiomatic: Wanshi is negligent in office—how can he govern the capital?"

sentences.zh: 請皆罷之。

translations.literal: I request that all be dismissed."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that all three be dismissed."

sentences.zh: ”似道大怒，黜文龍知撫州，旋又使台臣李可劾罷之。

translations.literal: Sidao was greatly angered, demoted Wenlong to prefect of Fuzhou, and soon had censor Li Ke impeach and dismiss him.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao was furious, demoted Wenlong to prefect of Fuzhou, and soon had censor Li Ke impeach him out of office.

sentences.zh: 未幾，呂文煥導大軍東下，範文虎首迎降，與文煥俱東。

translations.literal: Before long Lü Wenhuan guided the great army eastward; Fan Wenhu was the first to welcome surrender and went east together with Wenhuan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Lü Wenhuan led the Mongol army east. Fan Wenhu was first to surrender and marched east with him.

sentences.zh: 似道兵潰魯港，溍最先遁，以故列城從之皆遁，始悔不用文龍之言。

translations.literal: Sidao's army collapsed at Lugang; Jin was the first to flee, and for this reason the successive cities followed and all fled. Only then did he regret not using Wenlong's words.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao's army collapsed at Lugang; Jin fled first, and city after city followed. Only then did Sidao regret ignoring Wenlong.

sentences.zh: 起為左司諫，尋遷侍御史。

translations.literal: He was raised to Left Bureau Remonstrator and soon transferred to Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Left Bureau Remonstrator and soon promoted to attending censor.

sentences.zh: 時邊事甚急，王爚與陳宜中不能畫一策，而日坐朝堂爭私意。

translations.literal: At the time frontier affairs were very urgent; Wang Huo and Chen Yizhong could not devise a single plan, yet daily sat in court disputing private opinions.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier crisis was acute, yet Wang Huo and Chen Yizhong could agree on no policy and spent their days in court quarreling over private grievances.

sentences.zh: 潛說友以平江降，台臣請籍其家，爚以為可，宜中以為不可。

translations.literal: Qian Shuiyou surrendered Pingjiang; censors requested registering his household property. Huo thought it acceptable; Yizhong thought it not.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Shuiyou surrendered Pingjiang. Censors demanded confiscation of his family's property; Huo agreed and Yizhong refused.

sentences.zh: 張世傑諸將分四道出師，而大臣不監護，台諫論之，爚請行邊，下公卿雜議，宜中請出督師，又下公卿雜議。

translations.literal: Zhang Shijie's generals divided into four routes and marched out, yet the great ministers did not oversee them. Censors and remonstrators discussed it; Huo requested going to the frontier and submitted the matter to mixed deliberation among dukes and ministers; Yizhong requested going out to supervise the army and again submitted it to mixed deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shijie's generals marched out in four columns without ministerial oversight. Censors protested. Huo offered to inspect the frontier and referred the matter to the bureaucracy; Yizhong offered to supervise the armies and did the same.

sentences.zh: 文龍上疏曰：“《書》言‘三後協心，同底於道。

translations.literal: Wenlong memorialized, saying, "The Documents say, 'The three queens harmonize their hearts and together arrive at the Way.'"
translations.idiomatic: Wenlong memorialized: "The Documents say, 'Let the three queens join their hearts and walk together on the Way.'"

sentences.zh: ’北兵今日取某城，明日築某堡，而我以文相遜，以跡相疑，譬猶拯溺救焚，而為安步徐行之儀也。

translations.literal: The northern troops today take such-and-such a city, tomorrow build such-and-such a fort, while we yield to one another in words and suspect one another in deeds—it is like saving the drowning and rescuing from fire while performing the ritual of walking at ease in slow steps."
translations.idiomatic: The enemy takes a city today and builds a fort tomorrow, while we defer to one another in words and suspect one another in deeds—as if we were saving men from drowning and fire while insisting on walking at a ceremonial pace."

sentences.zh: 請詔大臣同心圖治，無滋虛議。

translations.literal: I request an edict that the great ministers join hearts in planning good government and not multiply empty talk."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Your Majesty command the ministers to unite in governing and cease empty debate."

sentences.zh: ”其後宜中與爚終不相能而去，至十月始來，事已不可為矣。

translations.literal: Afterward Yizhong and Huo could not get along to the end and left; only in the tenth month did he come, and affairs could no longer be accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhong and Huo remained at odds and stayed away; Yizhong did not return until the tenth month, by which time nothing could be saved.

sentences.zh: 是冬，累遷文龍至參知政事。

translations.literal: That winter Wenlong was repeatedly promoted to Vice Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Wenlong was promoted to vice councilor.

sentences.zh: 未幾議降，文龍乃上章乞歸養，既出國門而悔之，復上疏求還，不報，乃歸。

translations.literal: Before long surrender was discussed; Wenlong then memorialized begging to return home to care for his parents. After he had passed the state gate he regretted it, memorialized again asking to return, received no reply, and went home.
translations.idiomatic: When surrender was debated, Wenlong asked leave to retire and care for his parents. After he had left the capital he regretted it and petitioned to return; receiving no answer, he went home.

sentences.zh: 五月，益王稱製於福州，復以文龍參知政事。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Prince Yi assumed regency at Fuzhou and again made Wenlong Vice Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Prince Yi assumed the regency at Fuzhou and restored Wenlong as vice councilor.

sentences.zh: 漳州叛，以文龍為閩、廣宣撫使討之。

translations.literal: Zhang Prefecture rebelled; Wenlong was made pacification commissioner of Min and Guang to suppress it.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangzhou rebelled, Wenlong was made pacification commissioner of Fujian and Guang to suppress the revolt.

sentences.zh: 文龍以黃恮前守漳有恩信，辟為參謀官。

translations.literal: Wenlong, because Huang Shen had formerly governed Zhang with kindness and trust, summoned him as staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Wenlong recalled Huang Shen, who had once governed Zhangzhou with kindness, and made him his staff officer.

sentences.zh: 按兵泉州，使恮入招撫之，恮至，民皆頓首謝罪。

translations.literal: He held his troops at Quanzhou and sent Shen in to summon and pacify them. When Shen arrived the people all bowed their heads and begged pardon.
translations.idiomatic: He held his army at Quanzhou and sent Shen to win the people over. When Shen arrived they kowtowed in submission.

sentences.zh: 興化有石手軍者，能擲石中人，議者以其不足用罷之，石手軍亦叛，復命文龍為知軍，平之。

translations.literal: At Xinghua there was a Stone-Hand Army that could throw stones and hit men. Councillors thought them insufficiently useful and disbanded them; the Stone-Hand Army also rebelled. Wenlong was again ordered as military prefect and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Xinghua had a Stone-Hand corps skilled at throwing rocks. Court dismissed them as useless; they rebelled, and Wenlong was again sent as military prefect to crush them.

sentences.zh: 已而降將王世強復導大軍入廣，建寧、泉、福皆降。

translations.literal: Before long the surrendered general Wang Shiqiang again guided the great army into Guang; Jianning, Quan, and Fu all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the turncoat Wang Shiqiang guided the Mongol army into Guangdong; Jianning, Quanzhou, and Fuzhou all fell.

sentences.zh: 知福州王剛中遣使徇興化，文龍斬之而縱其副以還，使持書責世強、剛中負國。

translations.literal: The Fuzhou prefect Wang Gangzhong sent an envoy to proclaim authority at Xinghua. Wenlong executed him but released his deputy to return, sending him back with a letter rebuking Shiqiang and Gangzhong for betraying the state.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhou Prefect Wang Gangzhong sent an envoy to Xinghua. Wenlong executed him but let the deputy return with a letter denouncing Shiqiang and Gangzhong as traitors.

sentences.zh: 遂發民兵自守，城中兵不滿千，大兵來攻不克，使其姻家持書招降之，文龍焚書斬其使。

translations.literal: He then mobilized militia to defend himself; troops in the city were fewer than a thousand. The great army came to attack but could not take it. They had his in-law bring a letter to summon surrender; Wenlong burned the letter and executed the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: He mobilized the militia; the garrison numbered fewer than a thousand. The enemy failed to take the city. They sent his in-law with surrender terms; Wenlong burned the letter and beheaded the messenger.

sentences.zh: 有風其納款者，文龍曰：“諸君特畏死耳，未知此生能不死乎？

translations.literal: There were rumors that he would submit. Wenlong said, "You gentlemen merely fear death—you do not yet know whether in this life you can avoid dying."
translations.idiomatic: When rumors spread that he would surrender, Wenlong said, "You only fear death—you do not yet know whether you can escape it in this life."

sentences.zh: ”乃使其將林華偵伺境上。

translations.literal: He then had his general Lin Hua scout the border.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his general Lin Hua to scout the frontier.

sentences.zh: 華即降，且導兵至城下，通判曹澄孫開門降，執文龍與其家人至軍中，欲降之，不屈，左右淩挫之，文龍指其腹曰：“此皆節義文章也，可相逼邪？

translations.literal: Hua at once surrendered and moreover guided troops to below the walls. Vice Prefect Cao Chengsun opened the gates and surrendered. They seized Wenlong and his household and brought them to the army, wishing to win his surrender. He would not yield. Those at his side bullied and humiliated him. Wenlong pointed to his belly and said, "These are all integrity, righteousness, and literary composition—can you force them?"
translations.idiomatic: Lin Hua surrendered at once and guided the enemy to the walls. Vice Prefect Cao Chengsun opened the gates. They seized Wenlong and his family and tried to win him over. He refused. As they mocked him he pointed to his belly and said, "All this is loyalty and learning—can you force it out of me?"

sentences.zh: ”強之，卒不屈，乃械係送杭州。

translations.literal: They pressed him; in the end he would not yield and was shackled and sent to Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed him again and again; he never yielded and was sent in chains to Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 文龍去興化即不食，至杭餓死。

translations.literal: From the time Wenlong left Xinghua he did not eat; reaching Hang he starved to death.
translations.idiomatic: From the day he left Xinghua he refused food and starved to death at Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 其母係福州尼寺中，病甚，無醫藥，左右視之泣下。

translations.literal: His mother was bound in a nunnery at Fuzhou, gravely ill without medicine; those at hand wept to see her.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was held in a Fuzhou nunnery, desperately ill and without medicine. Those who attended her wept.

sentences.zh: 母曰：“吾與吾兒同死，又何恨哉？

translations.literal: The mother said, "I die together with my son—what regret is there?"
translations.idiomatic: She said, "I die with my son—what regret could I have?"

sentences.zh: ”亦死。

translations.literal: She too died.
translations.idiomatic: And she died.

sentences.zh: 眾歎曰：“有斯母，宜有是兒。

translations.literal: The multitude sighed, "With such a mother, it is fitting there should be such a son."
translations.idiomatic: People said, "Such a mother deserved such a son."

sentences.zh: ”為收葬之。

translations.literal: They gathered and buried her.
translations.idiomatic: They gave her a proper burial.

sentences.zh: 蒲壽庚以泉州降，告其民曰：“陳文龍非不忠義，如民何？

translations.literal: Pu Shougeng surrendered Quanzhou and told his people, "Chen Wenlong is not without loyalty and righteousness—but what of you people?"
translations.idiomatic: Pu Shougeng surrendered Quanzhou and told the people, "Chen Wenlong is loyal enough—but what about the rest of you?"

sentences.zh: ”聞者笑之。

translations.literal: Those who heard laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard laughed.

sentences.zh: 大兵既歸，文龍之侄瓚復舉兵殺林華，據興化，未幾復破，瓚死之。

translations.literal: After the great army had withdrawn, Wenlong's nephew Zan again raised troops, killed Lin Hua, and held Xinghua; before long he was again defeated and Zan died in it.
translations.idiomatic: After the Mongols withdrew, Wenlong's nephew Zan raised troops, killed Lin Hua, and seized Xinghua; he was soon defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 鄧得遇，字達夫，邛州人。

translations.literal: Deng Deyu, courtesy name Dafu, was a man of Qiong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Deyu, whose courtesy name was Dafu, came from Qiong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 淳祐十年進士。

translations.literal: Presented scholar in the tenth year of Chunyou.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in 1250.

sentences.zh: 調寧遠主簿，改知南昌縣，通判隆興府，監行在左藏庫，出知昭州，遷廣西提點刑獄，逾年攝經略事兼知靜江府。

translations.literal: He was assigned as registrar of Ningyuan, changed to magistrate of Nanchang County, vice prefect of Longxing Prefecture, overseer of the capital Left Treasury, sent out as prefect of Zhao Prefecture, transferred to judicial intendant of Guangxi, and after a year acted as pacification commissioner while concurrently governing Jingjiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as registrar of Ningyuan, then magistrate of Nanchang, vice prefect of Longxing, overseer of the capital Left Treasury, and prefect of Zhao before becoming judicial intendant of Guangxi. A year later he acted as pacification commissioner and concurrently governed Jingjiang.

sentences.zh: 德祐元年，長沙被兵，得遇遣都統馬驥、馬應麒赴援。

translations.literal: In the first year of Deyou Changsha came under attack; Deyu sent the commanders-in-chief Ma Ji and Ma Yingqi to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: In 1275 Changsha came under attack; Deyu sent commanders Ma Ji and Ma Yingqi to its relief.

sentences.zh: 驥潛叛而還，得遇斬之，軍事悉委之應麒。

translations.literal: Ji secretly rebelled and returned; Deyu executed him and entrusted all military affairs to Yingqi.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Ji secretly deserted and returned; Deyu executed him and gave Yingqi full command of the army.

sentences.zh: 未幾，馬塈代閫，議事不合。

translations.literal: Before long Ma Ji replaced him as commander of the circuit; they did not agree in council.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Ma Ji replaced him as circuit commander, and the two could not agree on policy.

sentences.zh: 二年，移治蒼梧。

translations.literal: In the second year he moved his administration to Cangwu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1276 he moved his headquarters to Cangwu.

sentences.zh: 靜江破，得遇朝服南望拜辭，書幅紙云：“宋室忠臣，鄧氏孝子。

translations.literal: When Jingjiang fell, Deyu in court robes faced south, bowed in farewell, and wrote on a sheet: "Loyal minister of the Song house, filial son of the Deng clan.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingjiang fell, Deyu in full court dress bowed south in farewell and wrote: "A loyal minister of Song, a filial son of the Deng clan.

sentences.zh: 不忍偷生，寧甘溺死。

translations.literal: Unwilling to steal life, I would rather gladly drown and die.
translations.idiomatic: I will not live in disgrace—I choose to drown.

sentences.zh: 彭鹹故居，乃吾潭府。

translations.literal: The old home of Peng Xian shall be my deep pool mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Xian's old dwelling shall be my deep pool home.

sentences.zh: 屈公子平，乃吾伴侶。

translations.literal: Master Ping of Qu Yuan shall be my companion."
translations.idiomatic: Qu Yuan's Master Ping shall be my companion."

sentences.zh: 優哉悠哉，吾得其所！

translations.literal: Easy and at ease—I have found my place!"
translations.idiomatic: At last I have found my place!"

sentences.zh: ”遂投南流江而死。

translations.literal: He then cast himself into the Nanliu River and died.
translations.idiomatic: He threw himself into the Nanliu River and drowned.

sentences.zh: 張玨，字君玉，隴西鳳州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Jue, courtesy name Junyu, was a man of Longxi, Feng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jue, whose courtesy name was Junyu, came from Longxi in Feng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 年十八，從軍釣魚山，以戰功累官中軍都統製，人號為“四川虓將”。

translations.literal: At age eighteen he joined the army at Diaoyu Mountain; through battle merits he was repeatedly promoted to commander-in-chief of the central army, and men called him "the fierce general of Sichuan."
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he enlisted at Diaoyu Mountain and rose through battle to commander-in-chief of the central army; men called him "Sichuan's fierce general."

sentences.zh: 寶祐末，大兵攻蜀，破吉平隘，拔長寧，殺守將王佐父子。

translations.literal: At the end of Baoyou the great army attacked Shu, broke Jiping Pass, took Changning, and killed the defending general Wang Zuo and his son.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Baoyou era the Mongols invaded Sichuan, took Jiping Pass and Changning, and killed the defender Wang Zuo and his son.

sentences.zh: 至閬州，降安撫楊奫，推官趙廣死之。

translations.literal: Reaching Lang Prefecture, Pacification Commissioner Yang Shen surrendered; the supervising secretary Zhao Guang died for it.
translations.idiomatic: At Langzhou, Pacification Commissioner Yang Shen surrendered; the supervising secretary Zhao Guang died rather than submit.

sentences.zh: 至蓬州，降守將張大悅，運使施擇善死之。

translations.literal: Reaching Peng Prefecture, the defending general Zhang Dayue surrendered; the transport commissioner Shi Zeshan died for it.
translations.idiomatic: At Pengzhou, the defender Zhang Dayue surrendered; Transport Commissioner Shi Zeshan died rather than submit.

sentences.zh: 順慶、廣安諸郡，破竹而下。

translations.literal: Shunqing, Guang'an, and the other prefectures fell like splitting bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: Shunqing, Guang'an, and the surrounding prefectures fell in rapid succession.

sentences.zh: 明年，合諸道兵圍合州，凡攻城之具無不精備。

translations.literal: The next year they combined troops from all routes and besieged Hezhou; every instrument for storming cities was prepared to perfection.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Mongols mustered troops from every quarter and besieged Hezhou, with every siege engine made ready.

sentences.zh: 玨與王堅協力戰守，攻之九月不能下。

translations.literal: Jue and Wang Jian together exerted strength in fighting and defending; the siege lasted nine months but the city could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Jue and Wang Jian held the city together; the Mongols besieged it for nine months without success.

sentences.zh: 景定初，合守王堅征入朝，以馬千代守合。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingding, Hezhou defender Wang Jian was summoned to court; Ma Qian was made to replace him in defending He.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingding era Wang Jian was recalled to court and Ma Qian was left to hold Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，千子饋餉至虎相山，為東川兵所得，屢以書勸千降，朝廷乃以玨代千。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Qian's son bringing provisions reached Huxiang Mountain and was taken by Eastern Sichuan troops; they repeatedly wrote urging Qian to surrender, and the court then replaced Qian with Jue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Ma Qian's son was captured at Huxiang Mountain while bringing supplies; the enemy repeatedly urged Ma Qian to surrender, and the court replaced him with Jue.

sentences.zh: 玨魁雄有謀，善用兵，出奇設伏，算無遺策。

translations.literal: Jue was bold and heroic with stratagems, skilled in using troops, deploying surprises and setting ambushes; in calculation no plan was overlooked.
translations.idiomatic: Jue was bold and cunning, a master of arms who laid ambushes and surprises; his plans never missed.

sentences.zh: 其治合州，士卒必練，器械必精，禦部曲有法，雖奴隸有功必優賞之，有過雖至親必罰不貸，故人人用命。

translations.literal: In governing Hezhou, soldiers had to be trained, weapons had to be refined, and command of subordinate units had regulations; though a slave, if meritorious he would certainly be richly rewarded; though at fault, though the closest kin, he would certainly be punished without pardon—therefore every man obeyed orders.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Hezhou with iron discipline: troops drilled, weapons kept sharp, every unit under firm command. Slaves who earned merit were richly rewarded; even kin who broke the rules were punished without mercy, and every man fought to the order.

sentences.zh: 自全汝楫失大良平，大兵築虎相山，駐兵兩城，時出攻梁山、忠萬開達，民不得耕，兵不得解甲而臥，每餉渠，竭數郡兵護送，死戰兩城之下始克入。

translations.literal: From the time Quan Ruji lost Daliangping, the great army built on Huxiang Mountain and stationed troops at two cities; from time to time they came out to attack Liangshan, Zhong, Wan, Kai, and Da; the people could not plow, the troops could not remove armor to lie down. Whenever supplies were brought, troops were exhausted from several prefectures to escort them; only after dying in battle below the two cities could they enter.
translations.idiomatic: After Quan Ruji lost Daliangping the Mongols fortified Huxiang Mountain and garrisoned two forts, raiding Liangshan, Zhongzhou, Wanzhou, Kaizhou, and Dazhou. Farmers could not tend their fields; defenders slept in armor. Every supply convoy required troops from several prefectures to escort it, and men had to fight their way through the enemy camps before reaching the city.

sentences.zh: 鹹淳二年十二月，玨遣其將史炤、王立以死士五十斧西門入，大戰城中，復其城。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Xianchun, Jue dispatched his generals Shi Zhao and Wang Li with fifty death-defying soldiers to axe their way in through the west gate, fighting a great battle in the city and recovering the city.
translations.idiomatic: In December 1266 Jue sent Shi Zhao and Wang Li with fifty chosen men to break in through the west gate, fought through the city, and retook the fort.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，平章賽典赤提兵入，壞重慶麥，道出合城下，玨碇舟斷江中為水城，大兵數萬攻之不克，遂引去。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year, the counselor Sayan Ajir came with troops, ruined Chongqing's wheat, and passed the road below He City. Jue anchored boats blocking the river to make a water fortress; the great army of several tens of thousands attacked but could not overcome it, and then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In April 1267 the Yuan counselor Sayan Ajir led troops that ravaged Chongqing's wheat and passed below Hezhou. Jue moored boats across the river to form a water barrier; tens of thousands of Mongols failed to break it and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 合州自餘玠用二冉生策，徙軍釣魚山，城壁甚固。

translations.literal: Since Yu Jie's use of the Two Ran brothers' stratagem at Hezhou, the army had been moved to Diaoyu Mountain; walls and ramparts were very solid.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yu Jie had adopted the Two Rans' plan and moved the garrison to Diaoyu Mountain, Hezhou's walls were exceptionally strong.

sentences.zh: 然開、慶受兵，民凋弊甚，玨外以兵護耕，內教民墾田積粟，未再期，公私兼足。

translations.literal: Yet Kai and Qing had suffered warfare; the people were ravaged and exhausted. Jue outwardly used troops to protect plowing, inwardly taught the people to open fields and amass grain. Before two years were out, public and private were both sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Kaizhou and Qing Prefecture had been ravaged by war. Jue sent troops to protect the fields and taught the people to reclaim land and store grain; within two years public and private stores were full again.

sentences.zh: 九年，叛將劉整復獻計，欲自青居進築馬鬃、虎頂山，扼三江口以圖合，匣刺統軍率諸翼兵以築之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the rebel general Liu Zheng again offered a plan: to advance from Qingju, build at Mazon and Huding Mountain, choke the Three Rivers' mouth to scheme against He. The commander Xi'a led winged troops to build it.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the turncoat Liu Zheng proposed building forts at Mazon and Huding Mountain from Qingju to block the three rivers and threaten Hezhou; the commander Xi'a led wing troops to construct them.

sentences.zh: 左右欲出兵與之爭，玨不可，曰：“蕪菁平母德、彰城，汪帥勁兵之所聚也，吾出不意而攻之，馬鬃必顧其後，不暇城矣。

translations.literal: Those at his side wished to lead troops out and contest it; Jue would not allow it, saying, "Wujing Pingmude and Zhangcheng—these are where Marshal Wang's crack troops are gathered. If we attack by surprise, Mazon must look to its rear and have no leisure to build the walls.
translations.idiomatic: His officers urged a direct assault; Jue refused. "Wujing Pingmude and Zhangcheng are where Marshal Wang's best troops are massed," he said. "A surprise strike there will force them to abandon Mazon before the walls go up.

sentences.zh: ”乃張疑兵嘉渠口，潛師渡平陽灘攻二城，火其資糧器械，越砦七十里，焚工場，統製周虎戰死，馬工城卒不就。

translations.literal: He then displayed decoy troops at Jiaqu Pass, secretly crossed Pingyang Beach to attack the two cities, fired their supplies and equipment, passed the stockade for seventy li, burned the works, the commander Zhou Hu died in battle, and the Mazon fortification in the end was not completed.
translations.idiomatic: He feigned at Jiaqu Pass while secretly crossing Pingyang Beach to strike the two forts, burning their stores and equipment, raiding seventy li deep and burning the workshops. Commander Zhou Hu fell in battle and the Mazon fort was never finished.

sentences.zh: 時陽立以涪州降，玨遣張萬攻走立，俘其僚屬馮巽午等。

translations.literal: At that time Yang Li surrendered Fu Prefecture; Jue sent Zhang Wan to attack and drive Li away, capturing his subordinates Feng Xunwu and others.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Li surrendered Fuzhou, Jue sent Zhang Wan to drive him out and captured his subordinates including Feng Xunwu.

sentences.zh: 立復合兵來決戰，史進、張世傑戰死，萬不支，俘立妻子及安撫李端以歸。

translations.literal: Li again combined troops to come to decisive battle; Shi Jin and Zhang Shijie died in battle; Wan could not sustain it and captured Li's wife and children and Pacification Commissioner Li Duan to return.
translations.idiomatic: Li returned with reinforced troops for a pitched battle. Shi Jin and Zhang Shijie were killed; Zhang Wan was overrun but carried off Li's wife and children and Pacification Commissioner Li Duan.

sentences.zh: 玨以都統程聰守涪。

translations.literal: Jue made the commander-in-chief Cheng Cong defend Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Jue put Commander Cheng Cong in charge of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 重慶兵盡退。

translations.literal: Chongqing's troops entirely withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Chongqing's forces withdrew entirely.

sentences.zh: 玨聞二王立廣中，遣兵數百人求王所。

translations.literal: Jue heard Prince Yi had established himself in Guang and dispatched several hundred troops to seek the prince's whereabouts.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Prince Yi had set up court in Guangdong, Jue sent several hundred men to find him.

sentences.zh: 調史訓忠、趙安等援瀘州。

translations.literal: He transferred Shi Xunzhong, Zhao An, and others to relieve Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Shi Xunzhong, Zhao An, and others to relieve Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 張萬入夔，連忠、涪兵拔石門及巴巫砦，獲將士百餘人，解大寧圍，攻破十八砦。

translations.literal: Zhang Wan entered Kui, linked with Zhong and Fu troops to take Shimen and the Ba-Wu stockades, captured more than a hundred officers and soldiers, lifted the siege of Daling, and broke eighteen stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wan entered Kuizhou, joined forces from Zhong and Fu, took Shimen and the Ba-Wu stockades, captured over a hundred soldiers, lifted the siege of Daling, and stormed eighteen forts.

sentences.zh: 明年六月，張德潤復破涪州，執守將程聰。

translations.literal: The next year in the sixth month, Zhang Derun again broke Fu Prefecture and seized the defending general Cheng Cong.
translations.idiomatic: The following June Zhang Derun retook Fuzhou and captured the defender Cheng Cong.

sentences.zh: 先是，聰在重慶力主守城之議，玨入，不知也，使出守涪。

translations.literal: Earlier, Cong in Chongqing strongly advocated the plan to defend the city; when Jue entered he did not know of it and sent him out to defend Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Cheng Cong had strongly argued for holding Chongqing. Jue did not know this when he took command and sent him to hold Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 聰至郡怏怏，不設備，至是被執。

translations.literal: Cong reached the prefecture resentfully, made no preparations, and at last was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Cong took the posting in sullen resentment, neglected his defenses, and was captured.

sentences.zh: 德潤以肩輿載聰歸，語之曰：“若子鵬飛為參政矣，旦晚可會聚也。

translations.literal: Derun had Cong carried back in a sedan chair and said to him, "Your son Pengfei has become vice councilor; morning and evening you may meet and gather.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Derun had Cheng Cong carried off in a sedan chair and told him, "Your son Pengfei is now vice councilor—you will soon be reunited.

sentences.zh: ”聰曰：“我執彼降，非吾子也。

translations.literal: Cong said, "I am captured and he surrendered—he is not my son.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Cong said, "I am a prisoner while he surrendered—he is no son of mine.

sentences.zh: 是月，梁山軍袁世安降。

translations.literal: That month, Yuan Shi'an of Liangshan Army surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: That month Yuan Shi'an of the Liangshan garrison surrendered.

sentences.zh: 十月，萬州破，殺守將上官夔。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Wan Prefecture was broken; the defending general Shangguan Kui was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Wanzhou fell and its defender Shangguan Kui was killed.

sentences.zh: 十一月，瀘州食盡，人相食，遂破之，安撫王世昌自經死。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Lu Prefecture's food was exhausted; men ate one another, and it was then broken; Pacification Commissioner Wang Shichang hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Luzhou ran out of food and people resorted to cannibalism. The city fell and Pacification Commissioner Wang Shichang hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 大兵會重慶，駐佛圖關，以一軍駐南城，一軍駐朱村坪，一軍駐江上。

translations.literal: The great army assembled at Chongqing, stationed at Fotu Pass, with one army stationed at the south city, one army at Zhucunping, and one army on the river.
translations.idiomatic: The Mongol army converged on Chongqing, holding Fotu Pass with detachments at the south wall, Zhucunping, and the river.

sentences.zh: 遣瀘州降將李從招降，玨不從。

translations.literal: They sent the Luzhou surrendered general Li Cong to summon surrender; Jue would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: They sent the Luzhou turncoat Li Cong with surrender terms; Jue refused.

sentences.zh: 十二月，達州降將鮮汝忠破鹹淳皇華城，執守將馬堃，軍使包申巷戰死。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the Dazhou surrendered general Xian Ruzhong broke Xianchun Huanghua City, seized the defending general Ma Kun, and the army commander Bao Shenxiang died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the Dazhou turncoat Xian Ruzhong took Huanghua City, captured the defender Ma Kun, and Army Commander Bao Shenxiang was killed.

sentences.zh: 至元十五年春，玨遣總管李義將兵由廣陽，一軍皆沒。

translations.literal: In spring of the fifteenth year of Zhiyuan, Jue dispatched the overseer Li Yi leading troops by way of Guangyang; the whole army perished.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1278 Jue sent Overseer Li Yi through Guangyang with a detachment; the entire force was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 二月，大兵破紹慶府，執守將鮮龍，湖北提刑趙立與製司幕官趙酉泰皆自殺。

translations.literal: In the second month, the great army broke Shaoping Prefecture and seized the defending general Xian Long; Hubei judicial intendant Zhao Li and the commissionerate staff officer Zhao Youtai both killed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the Mongols took Shaoping Prefecture and captured the defender Xian Long; Hubei Judicial Intendant Zhao Li and staff officer Zhao Youtai both took their own lives.

sentences.zh: 玨率兵出薰風門，與大將也速

translations.literal: Jue led troops out the Xunfeng Gate and fought with the great general Yesü
translations.idiomatic: Jue led troops out the Xunfeng Gate to meet the great general Yesü

translations.literal: Jiaozhu)
translations.idiomatic: Jiaozhu)

sentences.zh: 兒戰扶桑壩，諸將從其後合擊之，玨兵大潰。

translations.literal: Er fought at Fusang Dam; the generals joined from behind in combined attack and Jue's troops were greatly routed.
translations.idiomatic: Er at Fusang Dam; the generals closed from behind and routed Jue's army.

sentences.zh: 城中糧盡，趙安以書說玨降，不聽。

translations.literal: Food in the city was exhausted; Zhao An used a letter to persuade Jue to surrender; he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: When the city's grain ran out Zhao An urged Jue to surrender in a letter; he refused.

sentences.zh: 安乃與帳下韓忠顯夜開鎮西門降。

translations.literal: An then with his subordinate Han Zhongxian at night opened the west gate and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao An and his man Han Zhongxian opened the west gate by night and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 玨率兵巷戰不支，歸索鴆飲，左右匿鴆，乃以小舟載妻子東走涪。

translations.literal: Jue led troops in street fighting but could not sustain it; returning he sought poison to drink; those at his side hid the poison. He then used a small boat to carry wife and children east fleeing to Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Jue fought house to house until he could hold no longer. He searched for poison, but his attendants had hidden it. He put his family in a small boat and fled east toward Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 中道大憾，斧其舟欲自沉，舟人奪斧擲江中，玨踴躍欲赴水，家人挽持不得死。

translations.literal: Midway he greatly regretted; he axed his boat wishing to sink himself; the boatman snatched the axe and cast it into the river; Jue leaped wishing to go into the water; family members pulled and held him so he could not die.
translations.idiomatic: Midstream he was overcome with remorse and tried to sink the boat, but the boatman wrested away the axe and threw it in the river. Jue leaped for the water, but his family held him back from death.

sentences.zh: 明日，萬戶鐵木兒追及於涪，執之送京師。

translations.literal: The next day the tümen commander Tiemuer caught up with him at Fu, seized him, and sent him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the Yuan commander Tiemuer overtook him at Fuzhou, captured him, and sent him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 重慶降，製機曹琦自經死，張萬、張起岩出降。

translations.literal: Chongqing surrendered; the commissionerate officer Cao Qi hanged himself; Zhang Wan and Zhang Qiyan came out and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Chongqing fell; Commissioner Cao Qi hanged himself; Zhang Wan and Zhang Qiyan surrendered.

sentences.zh: 進攻合州，破外城。

translations.literal: They advanced to attack Hezhou and broke the outer city.
translations.idiomatic: They pushed on to Hezhou and broke the outer wall.

sentences.zh: 三月，王立亦降。

translations.literal: In the third month, Wang Li also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Wang Li surrendered as well.

sentences.zh: 玨至安西趙老庵，其友謂之曰：“公盡忠一世，以報所事，今至此，縱得不死，亦何以哉？

translations.literal: Jue reached the Zhao Laonian hermitage in Anxi; his friend said to him, "My lord served with full loyalty throughout life to requite what you served—now reaching here, even if you may not die, what then?
translations.idiomatic: At the Zhao Laonian Hermitage in Anxi, a friend said to Jue, "You have served with perfect loyalty all your life. Even if you are spared now, what would be left for you?

sentences.zh: ”玨乃解弓弦自經廁中，從者焚其骨，以瓦缶葬之死所。

translations.literal: Jue then undid his bowstring and hanged himself in the privy; his followers burned his bones and with a clay jar buried them at the place of death.
translations.idiomatic: Jue unstrung his bow and hanged himself in a latrine. His followers burned his bones and buried them in an earthen jar where he died.

sentences.zh: 趙立者，字德修，重慶人。

translations.literal: As for Zhao Li, courtesy name Dexiu, he was a man of Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Li, whose courtesy name was Dexiu, came from Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 第進士，以上書迕賈似道被謫。

translations.literal: He ranked as presented scholar; because memorializing offended Jia Sidao he was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi, he was exiled after a memorial offended Jia Sidao.

sentences.zh: 德祐初，起為太社令、湖北提刑。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Deyou he was raised as Director of the Imperial Altar and Hubei judicial intendant.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Deyou era he was restored as Director of the Imperial Altar and judicial intendant of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 使蜀趣諸將入衛，至重慶則昝萬壽已降，玨方城守為後圖。

translations.literal: Sent to Shu to urge the generals to enter and guard the throne, when he reached Chongqing Zan Wanshou had already surrendered; Jue was then defending the walls planning for later.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to Sichuan to hurry the generals to the emperor's defense, he reached Chongqing to find Zan Wanshou had already surrendered while Jue was still holding the walls for a counterstroke.

sentences.zh: 立無以復命，還至涪，沉水死。

translations.literal: Li had no means to report back on his mission; returning to Fu he drowned himself in the water.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to report back, Zhao Li returned to Fuzhou and drowned himself.
